Co-constraints fix OBX-2 to one exact value, which contradicts "accept both CE and CWE" and "responses SHOULD use CE". Every co-constraint row tests OBX-2 for an exact value (for example 'CE'). A submitter that sends CWE for a coded observation fails validation, although the narrative says systems SHALL accept both. Patient Condition (75323-6) is fixed to 'CWE' in Z22, Z32, and Z42, while every other coded observation is 'CE'. An IIS that follows the narrative's SHOULD (use CE in responses) fails Z32/Z42 validation for that observation. Free-text Comment (48767-8) is 'CE' in Z22 but 'ST' in Z32.
recommendation: Yes, it needs to be reflected (comment 28). Allow both CE and CWE where the narrative says both are accepted (a value-set check on OBX-2 instead of exact text), or narrow the narrative. Set 48767-8 to a text type (ST or TX) in every profile. Decide whether 75323-6 should be CE like the rest.

message: Newborn ('NB') names are not held to the family-and-given rule, and other names are over-constrained when an 'L' name is present. The profiles implement the two XPN flavors by slicing the whole PID segment on PID-5.7, not by name repetition. If any repetition is 'L', every repetition (nickname, maiden, and so on) must use XPN_IZ01 and have both family and given name. If no repetition is 'L', every repetition uses XPN_IZ02, where only one of family or given is needed, so an 'NB' placeholder name with one part passes. The two slice conditions also overlap: a patient with an 'L' and an 'N' name matches both. Slicing exists only in Z22; the response profiles (Z31, Z32) always use PID_IZ01 and Z42 uses PID_IZ02.
recommendation: Statement (2) exists: XPN.7 is R in every PID-5 flavor. Statement (1) holds for 'L' only. Ask IGAMT whether a slice or co-constraint can apply per repetition (by XPN.7). If not, use a conformance statement such as "each PID-5 repetition with XPN.7 in ('L','NB') SHALL value XPN.1 and XPN.2". Make the two slice conditions mutually exclusive. Decide whether responses should follow the same rule. Statement (3) has no counterpart in the narrative yet; the card should state it once the data type pages exist.

message: Patient conditions: the text uses 30945-0 in the no-vaccination group; the profiles only allow 75323-6 there. Section 4.8.6.2 says conditions are sent as 30945-0 (contraindication/precaution) observations in an ORC/RXA group that reports no vaccination. Section 4.4.4.4 and Figure 20 say patient conditions use 75323-6 in the Patient Observations group. The co-constraint tables follow 4.4.4.4: in the no-vaccination (CVX 998) group, 30945-0 is not allowed, and 75323-6 (with 85585-8 and 88878-4) is. 30945-0 is only allowed in the contraindicated group (NA with a real CVX).
recommendation: CDC decides which representation is current, then aligns sections 4.4.4.4 and 4.8.6, Figure 20, and the co-constraint tables.

message: IZ-41 and IZ-42 on the shared MSH flavor apply to every message, and no message can pass both. All eight profiles use one MSH flavor, MSH_#ConsolidatedIG_IZ01. It carries IZ-41 (MSH-16 SHALL be 'AL') and IZ-42 (MSH-15 SHALL be 'NE') as segment-level constraints, so both apply to VXU, QBP, ACK, and RSP alike. The drafted examples follow the usual pattern (VXU and QBP with MSH-15 'ER' and MSH-16 'AL'; ACK and RSP with 'NE'/'NE'), and every one fails one of the two. Z22 also has its own message-level IZ-41 with slightly different wording.
recommendation: Move the acknowledgment-type constraints to the message profiles that need them (for example, VXU and QBP: MSH-16 'AL'; ACK and RSP: MSH-15 and MSH-16 'NE'), and say in the narrative which values each message uses. The example checks skip IZ-41 and IZ-42 until this is fixed (quality/config.yml).

section_title: Use of Administered vs. Historical on Output
message: Text says RSP should leave RXA-9 empty; Z32 and Z42 require RXA-9 for completed doses. The narrative prefers an empty RXA-9 in responses. In Z32 and Z42, RXA-9 is conditional and becomes Required whenever RXA-20 is CP or PA, which is every administered or historical dose returned. An IIS that follows the preferred approach fails validation.
recommendation: CDC decides. Either change the response flavors to make RXA-9 O (or RE) in Z32/Z42, or replace the narrative's preference with what to send (for example, always '00' or '01').

section_title: Z42 - Return Evaluated Immunization History and Forecast
message: Z42's co-constraint table has no conditions, so every history dose needs a forecast group. Z22 and Z32 select a co-constraint table by the kind of Order Segment Group (administered, refused, …). Z42 has one unconditional table. Its "Immunization Forecast Results" group is R [1..*], so it applies to every ORC/RXA group in the response: each returned dose would need a forecast, and evaluation results are allowed in the forecast group. Z42 also has no rows for eligibility, funding, VIS, comments, or contraindications, which Z32 returns.
recommendation: Make the Z42 tables conditional like Z32: evaluation for administered or historical doses (RXA-20 CP or PA), and forecast for the CVX 998 group. Add the event-level observations that Z32 allows.

message: The Order Segment Group flavors (text and Figure 20) and the co-constraint tables do not match. The flavor sections and Figure 20 list which observations belong in each Order Segment Group. The co-constraint tables allow more in some places and less in others. Main differences: serological immunity, history of disease, and patient condition are allowed in the administered and historical event groups (the text puts them only in Patient Observations). In Z32 they are allowed in every group. The contraindication set is required in Figure 20 but optional in the tables. Indication observations are missing from the historical-event table. Z32, the history-only response, has evaluation and forecast groups. Z42 has a single table with no conditions (see the Z42 finding). The cell-by-cell comparison is on the comparison page.
recommendation: Agree with CDC which is intended, then align both. The text and Figure 20 are the more restrictive and readable statement, so the tables probably need to change. Once aligned, generate the figure from the co-constraint tables so they cannot drift apart again.

message: The refusal slice also requires RXA-6 = 999, which the refusal section does not list. The Z22 slicing selects the refusal flavor (RXA_IZ01_Ref) only when RXA-20 = 'RE' and RXA-6 = '999', and constraint IZ-48 requires RXA-6 = 999 whenever RXA-20 = 'RE'. The refusal section's list of minimum elements leaves out RXA-6. A refusal sent with any other amount is not validated against the refusal flavor (so RXA-18 is not checked as required) and fails IZ-48. The same applies to contraindicated (NA, CVX ≠ 998) and no-vaccination (NA, CVX 998) groups, which both also select on RXA-6 = 999.
recommendation: The slicing is set up consistently with IZ-45 and IZ-48. Add "RXA-6 = 999 – Administered amount" to the refusal list, and state the RXA-6/ORC-3 values in the non-administration sections too. Consider whether the slice should key on RXA-20 alone, so that a wrong RXA-6 is reported by IZ-48 rather than silently changing which flavor applies.

message: "A SNOMED CT code from PHVS_VaccinationContraindication_IIS", but 12 of the value set's 23 codes are not SNOMED CT. The value set mixes 11 SNOMED CT codes with 12 CDC PHIN VS (CDCPHINVS) codes. A sender can use a CDCPHINVS code and pass validation while breaking the narrative's SHALL; or follow the narrative and be unable to express the concepts that only have CDCPHINVS codes.
recommendation: Say "a code from the PHVS_VaccinationContraindication_IIS value set", or update the value set to SNOMED CT only.

section_title: Dose Validity and Reason for Validity
message: "Y or N are the only allowable values" for dose validity is not enforced. The dose-validity observation (59781-5) is typed ID with no value set in the Z32 and Z42 co-constraints, so any value passes.
recommendation: Bind OBX-5 for 59781-5 to HL70136_IZ01 (or an equivalent Y/N value set).

message: Forecast observations: the text and the Z42 table list different LOINC codes. The narrative allows the legacy 30979-9 (Vaccines Due Next) after 30956-7, but the Z42 forecast group has no row for it, so it cannot be sent. The Z42 forecast group allows 93123-8 and 93122-0, which the Forecast section (4.4.4.6) does not mention. The status observation 59783-1 is bound to Imm_status in Z32 but has no binding in Z42.
recommendation: Add 30979-9 to the forecast group (optional), describe 93123-8 and 93122-0 in 4.4.4.6, and bind 59783-1 in Z42.

message: ORC-12 (Ordering Provider) has usage C with no predicate. In ORC_IZ01 (Z22, Z32), ORC-12 is conditional, but there is no predicate, so neither readers nor validators know when it is required. Z42's ORC_IZ02 has it as O.
recommendation: Add the intended predicate, or set a fixed usage.

message: The text allows a time-zone offset in PID-7; the profiles reject one. PID-7 uses TS_NZ, whose time pattern (DTM_NZ) has no offset, so a birth date/time with an offset fails format validation. The narrative tells senders to use the birth time zone and tells IIS to ignore any offset present. RXA-3 and OBX-14 also use TS_NZ. Their wording ("use the local time zone") is consistent if it means local time without an offset.
recommendation: Say "local time of birth, without a time-zone offset" in the narrative. If offsets must be tolerated, loosen the flavor. Align Z42 with the other profiles.

message: "Use the CDCREC value set": the profiles bind category-only value sets, without MENA or the detailed codes. The narrative talks about "the CDCREC value set", including detailed subcategories and Middle Eastern or North African (MENA) as a top-level race category. The profiles bind PID-10 to PHVS_RaceCategory_CDC_NullFlavor (6 OMB categories, Other Race, and three unknown codes) and PID-22 to PHVS_EthnicityGroup_CDC_Unk. Neither contains MENA or any detailed code. Both are Static/Open, so a validator would likely only warn, but readers cannot see what is allowed.
recommendation: Name the bound value sets in the narrative (or rename them in IGAMT). Decide whether MENA and the detailed CDCREC codes belong in the binding (Dynamic), and whether 2131-1 Other Race remains.

message: "SHALL populate RXA-11" for administered doses, but the administered flavor has RXA-11 as RE. The narrative makes RXA-11 mandatory for administered vaccinations. In the administered flavor (RXA_IZ01_Adm) RXA-11 is RE, so a message without it passes validation. RXA-11.4 (Facility) is R within LA2_IZ01, which only applies when RXA-11 is sent.
recommendation: Make RXA-11 R in the administered flavor (and the RE side of the RXA_IZ01 predicate R), or soften the statement to SHOULD. With usage "R" now defined as "IIS reports an ERR if missing", R matches the intent.

message: Co-constraint tables use usage 'S', which the guide does not define. Eighteen co-constraint rows and groups have usage 'S' (for example, VIS groups, the contraindication group, and the forecast dates). The guide defines R, RE, O, C, X, and IX. A reader cannot tell whether 'S' means "should", "situational", or something else, and Figure 20 shows these items as Required.
recommendation: Define 'S' in this section (as IGAMT uses it), or replace it in the tables with a defined usage.

Profile names are not consistent: Z44 "Z44-REQUEST EVALUATED IMMUNIZATION HISTORY AND FORECAST QUERY PROFILE", Z31 "Z31-RETURN A LIST OF CANDIDATES PROFILE" end in "Profile" or "Query Profile"; the others do not. All names are in capitals.

Segment flavor(s) OBX_IZ01, OBX_IZ02, OBX_IZ03 are defined but not used by any message (the messages use generated co-constraint copies instead). Pages for these would confuse readers; they can be hidden or removed.

MIROW guide Consolidating Demographic Records and Vaccination Event Records (BR202, BR203 - Retain all past IIS patient IDs; use the current one): Partly covered. The guide requires the current SR or LR in every RSP (as BR203 asks), but says retired identifiers "may be retained as aliases, but a complete identifier history is not required". Submitters are told they can store the IIS identifier (from code 5044 or an RSP) and use it in later queries; after a merge, the one they hold may be retired. The guide does not say whether a query naming a retired SR or LR finds the merged record.
recommendation: CDC to decide whether an IIS SHOULD resolve a retired SR or LR in QPD-3 to the current record (which MIROW BR202 makes possible), and to say so in Identifier Changes, Merges, and Retirement.

message: MIROW guide Consolidating Demographic Records and Vaccination Event Records (BR701, BR5301 - Elements with a single value): Partly covered. The profiles allow one value for each of these except the lot number: RXA-15 is required and repeats (1..*) in the administered RXA, and the guide does not say what a second lot number means. The SISC comparison found the same gap (sisc-lot-01).
recommendation: State that RXA-15 carries the lot number of the unit administered, and either limit it to one repetition or define what further repetitions carry (for example, a diluent or a separately supplied adjuvant).

message: MIROW guide Consolidating Demographic Records and Vaccination Event Records (BR1201, BR6001, P10 - Unmerge, and prevent re-merging (twins)): Missing. Unmerging is IIS processing, but the message is where twins are told apart: the multiple birth indicator (PID-24, RE) and birth order (PID-25, conditional). The narrative never mentions them, so submitters have no reason to send them. MIROW also treats them as values from Vital Records, the definitive source (BR601).
recommendation: Add a short section on multiple births to Patient Information: send PID-24 and PID-25 whenever known, because they are what keeps an IIS from merging twins, and query with them when known.

message: MIROW guide MIROW Common Vocabulary (Administered/Historical Indicator): Partly covered. The guide has two definitions that don't match. Key Terms defines an administered vaccination as "a dose reported by the system that directly recorded the vaccination event and knows its details". That is about who recorded it. Administered Vaccinations says administered vaccinations "SHALL represent doses given directly by the reporting organization", which is about who gave it. MIROW and RXA-9 code 00 (new immunization record) go with the second. Under the Key Terms wording, a clinic that types another clinic's dose into its own EHR "directly recorded" it.
recommendation: Change the Key Terms definition of Administered Vaccination to match Administered Vaccinations and MIROW: a dose reported by, or on behalf of, the organization that gave it. Define Historical Vaccination as any dose reported by another party.

message: MIROW guide Data Quality Assurance in Immunization Information Systems (BR001 - Minimum/mandatory data elements (BR001 table)): Partly covered. Most of the list is required in the guide (MSH-4, PID-5, PID-7, RXA-3, RXA-5, RXA-9, and RXA-11 for administered doses). Two elements differ. The recording organization, mandatory for a historical submission in MIROW, is ORC-17 in the guide, which is RE and which the guide says IIS "generally do not treat ... as a condition for message acceptance", adding that its usage may be reconsidered if adoption stays limited. The Vital Records elements (birth certificate number, birth facility) are not discussed; Vital Records feeds are outside the guide's main use cases.
recommendation: CDC to decide whether the guide should expect ORC-17 for historical vaccinations, as MIROW does, or say why not. Either way, the ORC-17 section should note that MIROW treats the recording organization as mandatory for historical submissions.

message: MIROW guide Data Quality Assurance in Immunization Information Systems (BR110 - Valid calendar dates in a submission): Missing. The guide requires RXA-3 to be the calendar date of administration but does not say what to send when only the month and year of a historical dose are known, which is common with vaccine cards and patient recall.
recommendation: CDC to decide how a historical vaccination with an unknown day is reported (the 15th of the month, following MIROW BR110, or a month-precision date), and say it in Historical Vaccinations or Date of Vaccination (RXA-3).

message: MIROW guide Data Quality Assurance in Immunization Information Systems (BR120 - Combination vaccine reported as single vaccination event): Missing. The guide does not say this for U.S. combination vaccines. The only statement on combinations is the opposite case: a foreign combination product with no CVX code SHOULD be decomposed into its component antigens, one vaccination event each. Without the general rule, a reader could take the foreign-product rule as the norm.
recommendation: In the CVX section, state that a combination vaccine is reported as one RXA with the combination's CVX (MIROW BR120), and make clear that decomposing into components applies only to foreign products with no CVX code.

message: MIROW guide Data Quality Assurance in Immunization Information Systems (BR127 - Vaccination event dosage): Partly covered. RXA-6 and RXA-7 are required in the administered RXA flavor, but the narrative says nothing about either beyond listing dose volume as a non-identifying field, and does not say how to send an unknown amount. MIROW's remark relies on the Release 1.5 convention of 999.
recommendation: State in the guide that RXA-6 carries the dose volume with its unit in RXA-7, and that 999 is sent when the amount is unknown (or decide otherwise), consistent with MIROW BR127.

message: MIROW guide Data Quality Assurance in Immunization Information Systems (BR129, BR130, BR132 - Lot number content (Appendix K)): Missing. The guide names lot number quality as a problem conformance cannot solve but says nothing about what RXA-15 should contain. RXA-15 may repeat in the administered flavor (for a unit-of-sale and a unit-of-use lot), which fits BR130 only if each repetition holds one lot number. ERR-5 code 3554 (lot number invalid) exists to report violations.
recommendation: Add to Non-Identifying Vaccination Fields (or the RXA-15 field notes) that each repetition of RXA-15 carries exactly one lot number as printed on the product, with no other text, and point to MIROW BR129-BR132 and Appendix K.

message: MIROW guide Data Quality Assurance in Immunization Information Systems (Comparison of past MIROW data quality best practices (published with the guide)): Conflict. The national ERR-5 code set cites MIROW rules by their old numbers. Seven codes cite numbers that now mean something else: 2001 (BR 118, now BR115), 2010 (BR 116, now BR126), 2016 and 2017 (BR 119, now BR128), 2018 (BR 101, now BR111), 2019 (BR 103, now BR113), and 2022 (BR102, now BR114). Three more cite numbers that do not match the code's content: 2214 cites BR 114 for the provider-type check (old BR113, now BR168), 2215 cites BR 130 for the license date range (old BR120, now BR133), and 2217 cites BR 113 for the patient name type. Code 2023 keeps the retired 14-day submission rule, which MIROW and this guide now put at 24 hours. Code 2024 cites a rule (medical contraindication) that MIROW retired.
recommendation: Ask AIRA, which maintains the code set, to cite the 2022 rule numbers (written "DQA2022 BRnnn"), to align code 2023 with the 24-hour expectation, and to decide whether code 2024 is still needed.

message: MIROW guide Immunization Information System Inventory Management Operations (BR704 (remarks), chapter 7 - Multi-component vaccines): Partly covered. The guide tells submitters to report the NDC of the lyophilized powder for reconstituted vaccines, and any NDC for other multi-component products. It says nothing about which lot number goes in RXA-15. RXA-15 repeats (1..*) in the administered RXA, so a submitter could send every component's lot, the outer package's, or one chosen at random. MIROW's answer is one lot number and one NDC from the outside of the package. The guide's NDC rule picks the powder, which serves product identification but not inventory. The same RXA-15 gap was found in the SISC and consolidation comparisons (sisc-lot-01, mirow-cr-08).
recommendation: CDC to decide which lot number a submitter sends in RXA-15 for a vaccine with several components: the one on the outer package that the IIS inventory knows (MIROW BR704), or the active component's, to match the NDC rule. Say so with the RXA-15 cardinality fix.

message: MIROW guide Management of Patient Status in Immunization Information Systems (Chapter 7, Table 8 - Coding provider-level status in HL7): Missing. The guide's patient status sections describe status only in general terms and never name PD1-16 or PD1-17, or say which code means what. The value set (HL70441) has the codes, with 'A' and 'I' required and 'L', 'M', 'P', and 'U' permitted, but a reader of the narrative cannot tell that 'M' is MIROW's "no longer a patient" or that 'P' signals a death.
recommendation: In Provider-Reported Status, name PD1-16 and PD1-17 and give MIROW's meaning for each HL70441 code (Table 8), including how 'P' relates to the deceased status.

message: MIROW guide Management of Patient Status in Immunization Information Systems (BR421, chapter 7 - Deceased): Partly covered. The guide makes deceased status take precedence and says it may be reported by providers or external death reporting, but does not name PID-29 and PID-30, or say how a death is reported in a VXU.
recommendation: In Deceased Status, state that a provider reports a death in PID-30 ('Y') with the date in PID-29, and point to MIROW BR421 for how an IIS confirms it.

message: MIROW guide MIROW Principles and Business Rules Reports (RR2009 - BR401 - Who is included in reminder/recall, including opt-out): Missing. PD1-11 (publicity code) carries the patient's reminder/recall preference. It is RE in the VXU, with twelve required national codes for what is allowed: none, reminder or recall only, by any method or no calls, or to the provider. PD1-18 carries its date. The narrative never mentions PD1-11. Submitters can't tell what the codes mean, that the field is separate from PD1-12 (sharing) and from patient status, or that an empty field means no preference was recorded. MIROW keeps opting out of reminder/recall separate from patient status (MPS2019 P313, P314; see mirow-mps-11).
recommendation: Add a short section on PD1-11 to Patient Information. Say that it records the patient's or guardian's explicit reminder/recall preference, with the date in PD1-18. Say that it is sent only when a preference was expressed, that it is independent of PD1-12 and of patient status, and that IIS use it to filter reminder/recall (MIROW RR2009 BR401).

message: MIROW guide Vaccination Level Deduplication in Immunization Information Systems (BR10 - Different lot numbers): Partly covered. The guide classifies lot number as non-identifying: a corrected lot number is sent as an update and SHOULD NOT by itself make the IIS treat the vaccination as new. That works when the IIS finds the earlier report through the submitting source and ORC-3. The guide says ORC-3 matching is not yet consistent, though, and an IIS that falls back to MIROW evaluation will see two records with different lot numbers and, under BR10, keep both. The two documents are not in conflict, but the guide does not say how they fit together.
recommendation: In IIS Matching and Correction Processing, say that an update is applied to the source record it identifies (by source and ORC-3, or the identifying fields) before deduplication is considered, so that MIROW's lot number rule does not turn a lot number correction into a second event.

message: MIROW guide Immunization Information Systems Patient-Level De-duplication Best Practices (Chapter 1 and chapter 5 - The report as a reference for patient deduplication): Missing. The guide cites MIROW's vaccination-level deduplication guide for "patient and vaccination record deduplication", but that guide covers only vaccination events. This report is the one that covers patients.
recommendation: Covered by the recommendation in mirow-vd-01 to cite this report in Record Consolidation and Deduplication.

message: MIROW guide Immunization Information Systems Patient-Level De-duplication Best Practices (Table 1.1, 5.2.1 (6) - Err on the side of preventing false merges): Reworded. The guide says high-confidence matches may be merged automatically and ambiguous cases reviewed, but not that a duplicate is the preferred error. The same point was made for vaccination events (see mirow-vd-04, whose recommendation should apply to patients as well).

MIROW guide Immunization Information Systems Patient-Level De-duplication Best Practices (4.1.2, 4.3.1, 5.2.1 (5) - Placeholder names for newborns): Guide adds. The guide supplies the national convention. A placeholder name is marked with name type 'NB' and never sent as the legal name. When the real name is known, the submitter sends both names together, along with the child's complete history, so the IIS can link the records.

MIROW guide Immunization Information Systems Patient-Level De-duplication Best Practices (3.6.1 - Fields used for matching): Partly covered. The guide covers names, date of birth, address, race, and ethnicity in detail. It doesn't discuss the multiple birth indicator or birth order (PID-24, PID-25), which this report lists as an optional matching field and MIROW's consolidation guide relies on to tell twins apart.
recommendation: Covered by the recommendation in mirow-cr-09 to add a short section on multiple births.

message: MIROW guide Consolidating Demographic Records and Vaccination Event Records (P03 - Make original information accessible): Reworded. The guide recommends keeping the link between each source record and the consolidated event, and allows keeping both the submitted and the cleansed address, but leaves retention of submitted values to the IIS.

MIROW guide Consolidating Demographic Records and Vaccination Event Records (BR204, BR702 - Retain past and multiple values): Reworded. The guide accepts repeated addresses, names, and contact methods and lets the IIS decide how many to keep; it does not recommend retaining past values. That is a reasonable split (retention is IIS policy), but the guide could point to MIROW for the reasons to retain them.

MIROW guide Consolidating Demographic Records and Vaccination Event Records (BR1002, BR5802, P12 - Do not overwrite validated data): Partly covered. The guide says IIS "are expected to apply these updates to the existing vaccination record", without the MIROW exception, although it also says returned values may differ from those submitted and that IIS must not require submitters to "correct" names. A submitter whose update is not applied has no way to know.
recommendation: CDC to decide whether the guide acknowledges that an IIS may keep a validated value instead of applying a resubmitted one (MIROW BR1002 and BR5802), and if so whether the ACK should report it as a warning.

message: MIROW guide Consolidating Demographic Records and Vaccination Event Records (BR601 - Supremacy of vital statistics): Reworded. Consistent with the guide's use of official documentation for the date of birth; the guide does not single out Vital Records or cover the other birth elements (see mirow-cr-09).

MIROW guide MIROW Common Vocabulary (The vocabulary as a whole): Missing. Key Terms says its terms "align with common usage in immunization and interoperability communities", and the data model uses the CDC Core Data Elements as its reference catalog. Neither mentions the MIROW Common Vocabulary, although the guide cites MIROW guides whose rules are written in its terms.
recommendation: In Key Terms, cite the MIROW Common Vocabulary. Add a short table mapping the guide's terms to MIROW's where they differ: submitting organization and submitter; administering organization and vaccinating organization; entering organization and recording organization; organization and provider organization or IIS-AO; funding eligibility and dose-level eligibility; funding source and dose-level public/private indicator; vaccination record and vaccination event.

message: MIROW guide MIROW Common Vocabulary (Submitter, Recorder, Vaccinator, IIS-Authorized Organization; notes on provider organization and IIS-AO): Reworded. The guide's roles line up with MIROW's: submitter is MSH-4, vaccinator is RXA-11.4, and recorder is ORC-17 (which the guide names "Entering (Recording) Organization"). The IIS assigns every organization identifier. The guide adds the responsible organization (MSH-22) and keeps the "accountable" wording MIROW questioned. When a message passes through an intermediary (an HIE, for example), MSH-4 names the organization on the connection. The message has no place for the other organizations in MIROW's chain of submission, so the IIS has to know them from onboarding.

MIROW guide MIROW Common Vocabulary (Immunization Contraindication, Immunization Exemption): Reworded. The guide discourages the unqualified term "contraindication". It treats patient characteristics as conditions and a decision not to give a dose as non-administration. That is a more precise split than MIROW's. A MIROW contraindication is a guide condition, and a MIROW exemption is closest to the guide's refusal.

MIROW guide MIROW Common Vocabulary (Dose-Level Eligibility, Dose-Level Public/Private Indicator, Lot-Level Public/Private Indicator): Reworded. The guide's terminology note gives the CDC Core Data Elements names and the LOINC codes, but not MIROW's names, which the decrementing inventory guide uses throughout (see mirow-di-04, mirow-di-05). Covered by the mapping recommended in mirow-cv-01.

section_title: Dose Validity and Reason for Validity
message: MIROW guide MIROW Common Vocabulary (Dose Condition): Partly covered. The guide has no way for a submitter to say that a dose it gave was substandard (expired, stored out of range, or given incorrectly). An IIS that learns of it shows it only as an invalid dose in the evaluation of the RSP. MIROW's decrementing guide records such a dose as "administered, non-viable" (S501), and the deduplication guide keeps the repeat dose and flags the invalid one (mirow-vd-15). The usual practice is to report the dose as given and let the IIS or the forecaster judge it, which may be enough.
recommendation: CDC to decide whether the guide should say how a submitter reports a dose it knows to be substandard (for example, a dose later found to have been stored out of range), or state that this is left to the IIS's evaluation.

message: MIROW guide Decrementing Inventory via Electronic Data Exchange (Introduction; Chapter 9 - HL7 immunization messaging): Missing. The guide says funding information is "primarily used for inventory decrementing and program operations" and that it supports "MIROW-aligned practices", but it cites neither this guide nor the MIROW guide on IIS collaboration with VFC (2011) that it builds on.
recommendation: In Funding Source and Eligibility, cite MIROW's Decrementing Inventory via Electronic Data Exchange (2016) as the best practice for using these elements to decrement inventory.

section_title: Vaccine Funding Source and Stock Models
message: MIROW guide Decrementing Inventory via Electronic Data Exchange (Chapter 3 - Vaccine storage models): Partly covered. The guide says U.S. jurisdictions "operate either a two-stock or three-stock inventory model" and that each IIS SHALL select one of the two. The universal model is covered by Universal Purchase and Default Eligibility. The guide does not mention the replacement model, in which the stock used is always private at the time of administration and eligibility alone drives replacement, nor say what funding source such providers send. A multi-stock jurisdiction can use the open value set's local extensions, but the guide does not say so.
recommendation: CDC to decide whether the SHALL in Vaccine Funding Source and Stock Models should allow a one-stock (replacement) model, and if so to say what funding source a provider in that model reports. Also say that fund types beyond the national codes (such as 317, CHIP, or state) are sent as published local extensions.

message: MIROW guide Decrementing Inventory via Electronic Data Exchange (BR204, S501 to S503, S1001 - Lot problems): Partly covered. The ACK rules give the right answer: the vaccination was recorded, so the VXU is accepted, and an issue that needs correction is a Warning. ERR-5 has codes for some of these cases: 2001 (expired vaccine administered), 2011 (lot not valid for the vaccine), and the general 2601 (inventory management error). But the guide never says that an inventory problem is reported this way. Submitters cannot tell from the guide whether a dose was decremented. Inventory and Accountability Considerations covers corrections only.
recommendation: Add to Inventory and Accountability Considerations that when a vaccination is recorded but inventory cannot be decremented (lot not found, inactive, expired, or at zero balance), the IIS SHOULD return a Warning with ERR-5 2601, or a more specific code such as 2001, so the submitter can correct the lot or account for the dose (MIROW BR204, P07).

message: MIROW guide Decrementing Inventory via Electronic Data Exchange (BR205, S1203, S1204 - Changes after a closed reconciliation): Reworded. The guide allows local policy to delay or review a correction "when inventory or accountability records can no longer be reconciled". The ACK says whether it was applied and whether manual follow-up is needed. An update or delete not applied for policy reasons is reported as Information, not as an Error. One consequence is not spelled out: correcting an identifying field such as RXA-3 means a delete followed by an add, which reverses and repeats the decrement and so can reach into a closed reconciliation period.

MIROW guide Decrementing Inventory via Electronic Data Exchange (Chapter 9 - Action codes and the vaccination ID): Guide adds. The guide provides that standard of practice. Submitters SHALL support A, U, and D, reuse the source record's ORC-3, and use a delete and add only when an identifying field changes. IIS treat source and ORC-3 as high-confidence evidence while still matching.

MIROW guide Data Quality Assurance in Immunization Information Systems (Introduction; Chapter 2 (data quality throughout the IIS lifecycle)): Reworded. The guide's data quality sections say the same thing in their own words and cite this MIROW guide as reference [5], but under the title "AIRA's IIS Data Quality Best Practices", which is not its title, and without saying that it is a MIROW best practice guide.
recommendation: Change reference [5] to the guide's title, "Data Quality Assurance in Immunization Information Systems" (MIROW, 2022), and name it in Data Quality Processes as the community's best practices for onboarding, incoming data, and data at rest.

message: MIROW guide Data Quality Assurance in Immunization Information Systems (BR173 to BR175 - IIS-AO IDs; P21 - Complete chain of submitting organizations): Reworded. The guide makes the IIS the authority for unique organization identifiers and gives each role its own field (MSH-4 submitting, MSH-22 responsible, ORC-17 recording, RXA-11 administering). Its model of the "chain" is narrower than P21: one submitting organization per authenticated connection, with intermediaries such as HIEs transparent. That is a reasonable message-level reading of P21, but the guide does not say so, and it does not carry BR174's advice against embedding changeable information in identifiers.
recommendation: In Implementation and Maintenance Considerations, add that identifiers should not embed information that can change, such as location or parent organization (MIROW BR174).

message: MIROW guide Data Quality Assurance in Immunization Information Systems (BR151 - Minimum date of birth; BR152 - Date of birth default): Missing. The guide says to use the date of birth from official documentation but not what to do when it is unknown. Note that MIROW's default for an unknown day is the 1st for a date of birth (BR152) but the 15th for other dates (BR110).
recommendation: In Date of Birth (PID-7), point to MIROW BR152 for patients who do not know their date of birth.

section_title: Accepted Code Systems for Administered Vaccinations
message: MIROW guide Data Quality Assurance in Immunization Information Systems (BR117 - Vaccine type CVX): Reworded. Same direction: the guide requires IIS to accept CVX and NDC and keeps CPT only for legacy interfaces. It puts NDC on the same footing as CVX for administered doses, which postdates the MIROW rule.

MIROW guide Data Quality Assurance in Immunization Information Systems (BR122 - Vaccine has vaccine product type): Reworded. The guide asks for complete product information, including NDC, on administered records when available, and requires submitters to support NDCs, but an IIS must accept an administered dose with only a CVX. That is the message-level form of a completeness rule, not a conflict.

MIROW guide Data Quality Assurance in Immunization Information Systems (BR137 - Administered/historical indicator should not be defaulted): Missing. RXA-9 is required, but the guide does not say what an IIS does when it is missing or invalid. Defaulting to "administered" would decrement inventory for doses the submitter did not give.
recommendation: Add that an IIS should not assume a value for a missing or invalid RXA-9, and should report it (ERR-5 3051 or 3551).

message: MIROW guide Data Quality Assurance in Immunization Information Systems (BR138 - Vaccine administrator and prescriber): Partly covered. The guide carries both people (RXA-10 administering provider, RE for administered doses; ORC-12 ordering provider, conditional) and says how to format their names, but not which identifier goes with them (license number, NPI, or a local ID), so the license number MIROW asks for has no stated home.
recommendation: CDC to decide whether the guide names an identifier for RXA-10 and ORC-12 (for example, NPI, with a license number as an alternative) or leaves it to local guides, and to say which.

message: MIROW guide Data Quality Assurance in Immunization Information Systems (BR145 - Allowed characters for names): Reworded. Consistent. The guide's rules are about preserving characters (spaces, hyphens, the 18 accented letters) rather than listing what is allowed; it does not say that digits or other symbols are invalid in a name.

MIROW guide Data Quality Assurance in Immunization Information Systems (BR148 - Patient first and last name two characters): Partly covered. The guide deliberately sets no minimum length ("typically defined by the IIS"), and says guidance may be added in a future version after community discussion.
recommendation: When minimum name length is discussed, start from MIROW BR148.

message: MIROW guide Data Quality Assurance in Immunization Information Systems (BR157 and BR158 - Patient phone number): Missing. The guide's phone and email sections cover which repetition and use code to send but not how the number itself is split across XTN components (country code XTN-5, area code XTN-6, local number XTN-7) or formatted. ERR-5 code 3532 (telephone number invalid) exists.
recommendation: Add to Phone and Email that the number is sent in XTN-5 to XTN-7 as digits only (MIROW BR157 and BR158).

message: MIROW guide Data Quality Assurance in Immunization Information Systems (BR159 and BR160 - Medical record numbers): Partly covered. The guide requires the primary exchange identifier to be stable and never reassigned, but does not mention the two common errors MIROW names: a newborn sent with the mother's identifier, and a Social Security number used as the identifier.
recommendation: In Primary Patient Identifier for Exchange, add that the identifier must not be the mother's identifier for a newborn, or a Social Security number (MIROW BR159 and BR160).

message: MIROW guide Data Quality Assurance in Immunization Information Systems (P18 - Vital Records): Reworded. Consistent: the guide asks for the date of birth from official documentation and recognizes death reporting from external sources; it does not name Vital Records as the authority.

MIROW guide Immunization Information System Inventory Management Operations (P701, BR701, BR702, chapter 7 - NDC supremacy, and finding the NDC from the lot number): Reworded. The guide keeps CVX as the canonical code and treats NDC as a SHOULD for administered doses, valuable for traceability and reconciliation. That fits MIROW's view that the IIS can derive the NDC behind the scenes. The guide accepts unit-of-use as well as unit-of-sale NDCs. An IIS that receives a unit-of-use NDC (the vial or syringe) still has to reach the unit-of-sale NDC for inventory, which MIROW does through the lot number. The guide doesn't say this, but it is IIS processing.

MIROW guide Immunization Information System Inventory Management Operations (P702, BR704 - A lot number for every administered dose): Reworded. RXA-15 is required in the administered RXA and optional in the historical RXA, which matches MIROW. But the guide does not let an IIS reject a vaccination only because the lot number is missing, unless the IIS has declared it Critical Data. The later MIROW guides take the same position: the 2016 decrementing guide records the vaccination and skips decrementing (S704), and the 2022 data quality guide makes the lot number recommended (BR131). So MIROW's 2012 rejection rule has been superseded.

MIROW guide Immunization Information System Inventory Management Operations (BR705 - Patient eligibility for every administered dose): Reworded. Eligibility is reported for each administered dose. A jurisdiction may enforce it for participants in public programs, but the guide prefers accepting the vaccination and following up. The 2016 decrementing guide (S701) and ERR-5 code 2500 take the same approach.

MIROW guide Immunization Information System Inventory Management Operations (BR706 - Organization responsible for the inventory): Partly covered. The guide defines the administering organization in RXA-11 as "the entity that physically administered the vaccine and managed its inventory", which assumes the two are the same. MSH-22 identifies the organization responsible for the data, not the inventory. Where they differ, nothing in the message says whose inventory to decrement. MIROW accepts that the IIS works this out from what it knows of the organizations.
recommendation: In Administering Organization (RXA-11), drop "and managed its inventory" or qualify it. Note that the inventory may belong to another organization (MIROW BR706), which the IIS determines from its records of the submitter's organizations rather than from the message.

message: MIROW guide Immunization Information System Inventory Management Operations (BR711 (remarks) - Lot number field used for other purposes): Partly covered. Now that funding source has its own OBX, there is no reason to put it in RXA-15. The guide doesn't say that RXA-15 carries only the lot number, as the 2022 data quality guide asks (see mirow-dqa-24).
recommendation: Covered by the recommendation in mirow-dqa-24. When adding it, say that stock designations belong in the funding source OBX, not in RXA-15.

message: MIROW guide Immunization Information System Inventory Management Operations (BR718, PM07 - Flag doses that do not match the inventory): Partly covered. The guide's ACK rules support this, but the guide does not say that an unmatched lot is reported. This is the same gap as mirow-di-12.
recommendation: Covered by the recommendation in mirow-di-12, which should cite MIROW 2012 BR718 as well as the 2016 guide.

message: MIROW guide Management of Patient Status in Immunization Information Systems (BR401, BR406 - Designations at the provider organization level): Reworded. The guide acknowledges the reasons but says they are "often operationally indistinguishable to IIS and should not be over-interpreted". That is consistent with MIROW's own note that many EHRs send no reason.

MIROW guide Management of Patient Status in Immunization Information Systems (P312 - Any submission should include patient status): Partly covered. The guide treats status as optional in practice: PD1-16 is RE, absence of a status is not evidence either way, and no IIS may make status a condition of acceptance. It does not ask submitters to send it, which MIROW does.
recommendation: Say that submitters SHOULD send PD1-16 (with PD1-17) when the provider maintains patient status, as MIROW P312 recommends, while keeping the rule that its absence means nothing.

message: MIROW guide Management of Patient Status in Immunization Information Systems (P308 - Explicit assignment takes precedence): Reworded. The guide treats provider-reported active and inactive values as "advisory rather than authoritative", which is weaker than MIROW's supremacy of an explicit assignment at the provider level. Both put deceased first.
recommendation: CDC to decide whether an explicit PD1-16 value from the provider should replace the provider-level status the IIS holds for that provider (MIROW P308), and say so, or explain why the guide treats it as advisory.

message: MIROW guide Management of Patient Status in Immunization Information Systems (P305 - Make status changes available to providers): Partly covered. The guide forbids transmitting jurisdictional or IIS-derived statuses in HL7 v2 messages, which is right for the jurisdiction level but leaves no message path for P305 at the provider level (for example, an IIS marking a patient inactive for a provider after a death confirmed by Vital Records). P305 can be met through reports or the user interface, but the guide does not say so.
recommendation: Add to IIS-Derived Status and Jurisdictional Views that IIS share provider-level status changes they make by other means, such as reports or the user interface (MIROW P305).

message: MIROW guide Management of Patient Status in Immunization Information Systems (Acceptance of vaccinations): Guide adds. The guide makes explicit that status is never a reason to refuse a vaccination, including historical data for a deceased patient.

MIROW guide MIROW Principles and Business Rules Reports (The report and spreadsheet): Missing. The guide cites individual MIROW guides but not the compiled rules, which are the stable way to point to a MIROW rule. The ERR-5 code set cites MIROW rules by bare number (BR 116) without the guide, which is how its citations became ambiguous (see mirow-dqa-45).
recommendation: Cite the MIROW Principles and Business Rules report among the references. Ask AIRA to cite rules in the ERR-5 code set by their full name (for example, DQA2022 - BR115).

message: MIROW guide MIROW Principles and Business Rules Reports (DLE2011 - BR614, BR615 - Which eligibility to report when several apply): Conflict. The national value set (V01 to V05 and V22 to V25) has one code per category, and the guide allows at most one value per dose. That supports MIROW's minimum set but not its best practice. The guide does not give the hierarchy for choosing among codes, so a patient who is both on Medicaid and AI/AN may be reported either way.
recommendation: CDC to confirm that only one eligibility value is sent per dose, which departs from MIROW's best practice (DLE2011 BR615). If so, add to Patient Funding Eligibility (Per Dose) that when more than one applies, the submitter reports the first in MIROW's order: V02 (Medicaid), V04 (AI/AN), V03 (uninsured), V05 (underinsured).

message: MIROW guide Patient Status in Immunization Information Systems: Recommendations and Implementation Strategies (Section 2 (provider level), Appendix D - The HL7 fields for patient status, and why EHRs don't send them): Partly covered. The guide's profile has all these fields, but its patient status sections don't name them. That is the gap the report describes. Covered by the recommendations in mirow-mps-02 (PD1-16, PD1-17) and mirow-mps-06 (PID-29, PID-30), and by mirow-pbr-07 for PD1-11.
recommendation: Apply mirow-mps-02 and mirow-mps-06, which bring MIROW's status codes into the guide that EHRs are certified against.

section_title: Patient Demographic Records and VXUs Without Immunizations
message: MIROW guide Patient Status in Immunization Information Systems: Recommendations and Implementation Strategies (Section 2 (EHR survey), Appendix D - Status changes are sent only with a vaccination): Partly covered. The guide requires IIS to accept a VXU with no vaccinations, but describes it for "correcting a patient's name, address, or date of birth on an existing immunization record, or updating demographic information in advance of an anticipated vaccination event". It also asks submitters to limit such messages and to use ADT where available. A provider reporting a death, or that a patient has moved or is no longer a patient, is not named as a reason. An EHR reading the guide could conclude it should not send one.
recommendation: In Patient Demographic Records and VXUs Without Immunizations, name reporting a death (PID-29, PID-30) and a change in the provider's patient status (PD1-16, PD1-17) as appropriate uses of a VXU without vaccinations.

message: MIROW guide Vaccination Level Deduplication in Immunization Information Systems (Introduction (scope)): Reworded. The guide cites this MIROW guide correctly in IIS Matching and Correction Processing, but its reference list ([10]) describes it as guidance on "patient and vaccination record deduplication". Patient deduplication is covered by CDC's Patient-Level De-duplication Best Practices (2013), which the guide does not cite.
recommendation: Correct the description of reference [10] to vaccination-level deduplication, and cite CDC's Patient-Level De-duplication Best Practices in Record Consolidation and Deduplication.

message: MIROW guide Vaccination Level Deduplication in Immunization Information Systems (BR09, P04 - Different until proven duplicate): Reworded. The guide says high-confidence matches may be merged automatically and ambiguous ones queued for manual review, but not that, when in doubt, keeping both records is the safer error. That bias matters to submitters, who otherwise may expect every resend to collapse into one record.
recommendation: Add to Record Consolidation and Deduplication that IIS deliberately prefer to keep two records rather than wrongly merge them (MIROW BR09), so occasional duplicates are expected.

message: MIROW guide Vaccination Level Deduplication in Immunization Information Systems (P10, Table 9 - Confidence in the data): Partly covered. The message carries this information: RXA-9 distinguishes a new administration (00) from historical records by source (from another provider, another registry, a written record, a school record, a birth certificate, a public agency, or the patient's recall, which the value set marks as low reliability). The narrative never mentions these codes or asks submitters to send the most specific one rather than 01 (source unspecified).
recommendation: In Historical Vaccinations, list the RXA-9 historical source codes, ask submitters to send the most specific source they know, and note that IIS use it to weigh records when deduplicating (MIROW P10).

section_title: Use of Administered vs. Historical on Output
message: MIROW guide Vaccination Level Deduplication in Immunization Information Systems (Use of the consolidated record in query responses): Guide adds. The guide returns the consolidated history, without administered/historical distinctions, and the source-assigned ORC-3 when it can.

MIROW guide Vaccination Level Deduplication in Immunization Information Systems (Corrections and deletes): Guide adds. The guide defines how submitters signal corrections (update for non-identifying fields, delete followed by add for identifying ones, reusing ORC-3), that a delete retracts one source record rather than the consolidated event, and that an IIS must not create a duplicate just because a correction was sent as an add.
Glossary entry "RCP" points to "RCP-2 definition in Z31 - Return a List of Candidates"; "RCP-2 definition" does not match a section title, so it cannot become a link.

SISC guidance Guidance on Unit of Sale/Unit of Use Lot Numbers (Document Use): Missing. The guide treats the same unit-of-use and unit-of-sale problem for NDCs, and IGAMT makes RXA-15 (lot number) required for administered doses, but the guide never says which lot number RXA-15 carries, or that it may differ from the inventory lot.
recommendation: State that RXA-15 carries the lot number of the unit administered (the vial or syringe), that for some products this differs from the unit-of-sale lot used for inventory, and link this guidance.

message: SISC guidance Guidance on Detailed Message Structure and the Use of Specific LOINC Codes (Change History (version 1.1)): Conflict. The guide's flavor sections follow this (30945-0 only in the Contraindicated group, which "links contraindication observations to a specific vaccine that was not given"), and so does IGAMT. But section 4.8.6.3 says conditions may be sent as standalone patient-level observations or in a not-administered group, that IIS process both "identically", and that RXA-20 = NA "does not create standardized meaning linking the condition to a specific non-administered vaccine". That reverses the reason for the v1.1 change. The representation conflict is already a finding (qf-igamt-condition-loinc); this adds the history CDC should weigh when deciding it.
recommendation: When deciding qf-igamt-condition-loinc, note that SISC moved contraindications into the Contraindicated group in 2018 precisely so the vaccine is identified. If the guide keeps 4.8.6.3, record the reversal in the change history.

message: SISC guidance Guidance on Populating OBX-14 (Populating OBX-14 (principles)): Reworded. Section 4.4.2.6 says OBX-14 should reflect when the observation "occurred or was recorded", adding "recorded". Section 4.8.6.3 says OBX-14 "represents the date the observation was authored or recorded" and "does not indicate when the underlying condition began", except for ongoing conditions. This guidance's summary is explicit that OBX-14 reflects the time of the observation "and not when the message is created".
recommendation: Drop "or recorded" in 4.4.2.6, and align 4.8.6.3 with it: OBX-14 is when the observation occurred (the onset for ongoing conditions). If CDC prefers the recording date for conditions, say so in 4.4.2.6 as an exception.

message: SISC guidance Guidance on Populating OBX-14 (Guidance for specific observation types (table)): Partly covered. The guide gives the rule for serology and multi-day conditions, but not the table. Without it, senders must guess the date for eligibility, funding source, VIS, comments, evaluations, and forecasts.
recommendation: Add the table to 4.4.2.6 (it is short), or put the date in each observation's row in Figure 20.

message: SISC guidance Guidance on Indicating Preferable and Contraindicated Vaccines (Scope of Guidance (In Scope)): Missing. The guide says these elements are used "cautiously and only when clinically justified", but not how a receiver should read them.
recommendation: Add that a preferred vaccine type is a recommendation, not a complete or mandatory list of products.

message: SISC guidance Guidance on Indicating Preferable and Contraindicated Vaccines (Expectations of Support): Partly covered. Both are MAY in the guide, so support is optional, and s4 asks IIS to document product guidance in their local IG. The safety warning is gone: a querying system that ignores unknown OBX segments is fine, but one that reads every CVX in a forecast set as recommended would show a contraindicated vaccine (93122-0) as due.
recommendation: State that IIS return these OBX segments only to querying systems that have agreed to receive them, and that querying systems SHALL NOT present a contraindicated vaccine type as recommended.

message: SISC guidance Query Responses and Patient Protection (Guidance when implementing Release 1.5): Missing. The guide says a Z32 or Z42 returns "the complete immunization history", but never addresses withholding some doses for privacy, or the clinical risk of a history that looks complete but is not.
recommendation: In the consent sections or the Z32/Z42 sections, state that an IIS SHOULD NOT return a partial history to protect some doses: it returns either the whole history or a Z33.

section_title: Z33 - Return a Response with No Person Records
message: SISC guidance Query Responses and Patient Protection (Guidance when implementing Release 1.5): Missing. The guide has a single Z33 for every case and no way to tell a querying system that a protected patient was found. The FAQ records why that matters: EHR systems may need to distinguish a protected patient from no patient (for example, so staff do not create a duplicate record or keep re-querying).
recommendation: Describe the "protected patient found" Z33 in the Z33 section, updated for this guide: MSA-1 'AA', one ERR segment with ERR-4 'I' and ERR-5 2700 (see sisc-qrpp-05), ERR-8 text for the user, and QAK-2 'NF' (or 'PD'; see sisc-qrpp-06). State that an IIS uses it only where law and policy allow it to reveal that the patient exists.

message: SISC guidance Query Responses and Patient Protection (Guidance for incorporation into a future release): Missing. The code now exists in the national set of ERR-5 codes: 2700 "Protected Patient Found" (and 2701 "Potentially Protected Patient Found"), both noted as applying to a single high-threshold match. The guide publishes that code set (Appendix D) but does not mention either code in its consent or Z33 sections.
recommendation: Name ERR-5 codes 2700 and 2701 in the Z33 section, as the way to tell a querying system that a protected patient was found.

section_title: Z33 - Return a Response with No Person Records
message: SISC guidance Query Responses and Patient Protection (Guidance for incorporation into a future release): Missing. Neither the guide nor IGAMT has 'PD': QAK-2 is bound to HL70208_IZ01 with OK, NF, TM, AE, and AR. 'PD' is not an HL7 v2.5.1 code, so adding it would extend an HL7 table. With ERR-5 2700 available, 'PD' may no longer be needed, but the FAQ said it would be added, so its omission should be a decision rather than an oversight.
recommendation: CDC to decide whether to add QAK-2 'PD' or rely on QAK-2 'NF' with ERR-5 2700. Record the decision in the change history.

message: SISC guidance Guidance for HL7 RSP Messages to Support Interoperability (Caveats): Partly covered. The guide defines the ERR-4 severities only in terms of a VXU and its core intent ("results in rejection of the submitted VXU because core intent was not fulfilled"). Nothing says the same severities apply to an RSP, or what "core intent" means for a query.
recommendation: State that the ERR-4 severities apply to query responses as well, and say what an Error means for a query (the query could not be executed and must be corrected and resent).

message: SISC guidance Guidance for HL7 RSP Messages to Support Interoperability (Query Response Guidance (message is rejected)): Partly covered. The guide's Z23 section describes the same outcome more broadly ("malformed or invalid MSH/QPD segments, missing required message header information, or other unrecoverable errors detected prior to query execution"), and figure 17 shows it as "Structurally valid? No". It does not name the four MSH conditions. The fifth condition, "unrelated to format or content", is one the guide removes as a reason for 'AR' on a VXU (following the ACK TAB), because it describes a transport problem. The guide does not say whether it is also removed for queries.
recommendation: Name the MSH conditions that lead to a Z23, and say that, as for VXUs, a transport or connectivity problem is never reported with a Z23.

message: SISC guidance Guidance for HL7 RSP Messages to Support Interoperability (Query Response Guidance (message is rejected)): Missing. The Z23 section says the IIS "is unable to execute the query" but not what MSA-1 and ERR-4 contain. The guide's MSA-1 rules ('AR' when there is a severity 'E' error) are written for a VXU ("SHALL be returned to convey VXU rejection"). The IGAMT Z23 profile allows either a Q11 or a V04 trigger, so the same profile serves both, but only the VXU case is described.
recommendation: In the Z23 section, state that a Z23 sent in response to a QBP has MSA-1 'AR' and one ERR segment with ERR-4 'E'.

section_title: Z33 - Return a Response with No Person Records
message: SISC guidance Guidance for HL7 RSP Messages to Support Interoperability (Query Response Guidance (error prevents the query)): Missing. The guide's Z33 section lists only no match, policy limits, and consent restrictions, and says that a Z33 means the IIS "has processed the query". Figure 17 has no path for a query that is accepted but cannot be executed. The combination this guidance requires also conflicts with the guide's new ACK model: for a VXU the guide says MSA-1 'AE' SHALL NOT be returned with a severity 'E' error, and that 'AE' means a qualified acceptance. If that model applies to query responses, a failed query would get MSA-1 'AR'; if it does not, the guide needs to say so.
recommendation: CDC to decide how a query that cannot be executed is reported: Z33 with MSA-1 'AE' as in this guidance, or Z33 (or Z23) with MSA-1 'AR' to match the ACK model. Then add the outcome to the Z33 section and to figure 17, with the QAK-2 value ('AE').

message: SISC guidance Guidance for HL7 RSP Messages to Support Interoperability (Query Response Guidance (query is successfully processed)): Missing. These rules agree with the guide's MSA-1 rules for VXUs ('AA' with no 'W' or 'E', 'AE' with 'W' and no 'E'), but the guide states them only for a VXU. Nothing in the RSP sections says how to populate MSA-1 in a query response.
recommendation: Say in the RSP sections that MSA-1 and ERR-4 in a query response follow the same rules as in an ACK, or state the RSP rules there.

message: SISC guidance Guidance for HL7 RSP Messages to Support Interoperability (Query Response Guidance (query is successfully processed); Summary): Missing. The guide never explains QAK-2 or how it relates to MSA-1. The only QAK-2 value it names is 'TM', in the Z31 section. The IGAMT profiles bind QAK-2 to HL70208 (OK, NF, TM, AE, AR) but set no rule linking it to the outcome or to MSA-1.
recommendation: Add a short section, or a table like this guidance's Table 2, on QAK-2: what each value means, which values go with which response profile, and that QAK-2 and MSA-1 are set independently.

section_title: Z31 - Return a List of Candidates
message: SISC guidance Guidance for HL7 RSP Messages to Support Interoperability (Summary (Table 2, footnote 1)): Partly covered. The Z31 section says that an IIS with too many candidates "returns a QAK-2 value of TM" rather than an oversized Z31, but does not say which response profile carries it (Z33), and does not allow 'NF' where policy forbids revealing that several patients match.
recommendation: Say that too many matches is reported with a Z33 and QAK-2 'TM', or 'NF' where local law or policy does not allow the IIS to reveal that several patients match.

message: SISC guidance Guidance for HL7 Acknowledgement Messages to Support Interoperability (MSA-1 (Acknowledgement Code), Tables 4 and 5): Conflict. Changed on purpose, following the ACK TAB. In the guide, 'AE' SHALL NOT be returned when there is an Error, 'AR' is returned whenever core intent is not fulfilled (any Error), and "unable to process for reasons unrelated to format or content" is no longer a reason for 'AR'. The guide's MSA-1 guidance explains the change but does not name this document. IIS and senders that built to the 2015 rules will send or expect 'AE' for rejected messages.
recommendation: In the change history, record that the MSA-1 rules replace those in the 2015 ACK guidance (and Release 1.5): 'AE' no longer covers rejections. Consider a short migration note for systems that treat 'AE' as a rejection.

message: SISC guidance Guidance on Unit of Sale/Unit of Use Lot Numbers (Notes: Matching, Reconstituted Vaccines, and Regular Expression): Out of scope. The guide deliberately "does not prescribe an IIS's internal inventory or lot-validation workflows", so this is IIS operations. Its inventory section would still benefit from a link to this guidance and to the MIROW inventory guide.
recommendation: In the inventory section, link this guidance and the MIROW guide on decrementing inventory (see the MIROW alignment proposal).

message: SISC guidance Guidance on Unit of Sale/Unit of Use Lot Numbers (Notes: Matching, Reconstituted Vaccines, and Regular Expression): Partly covered. The guide requires the NDC of the lyophilized powder rather than the diluent, but does not say the same for the lot number. A submitter could report the diluent's lot with the powder's NDC.
recommendation: Extend the reconstitution statement to the lot number: report the lot of the lyophilized powder (the active product), not the diluent.

section_title: Order Segment Groups and LOINC/OBX Grouping
message: SISC guidance Guidance on Detailed Message Structure and the Use of Specific LOINC Codes (Out of Scope): In narrative only. The guide says observations outside the defined flavors "must be interpreted based on local or bilateral agreements", and that IIS may support additional LOINC codes, but does not say an IIS should document them.

SISC guidance Guidance on Detailed Message Structure and the Use of Specific LOINC Codes (Structure of the VXU (Z22) message): Missing. The guide sets an order only for the RSP (the Forecast group comes last). It says nothing about where the Patient Observations group goes in a VXU or an RSP.
recommendation: State that the Patient Observations group, when present, follows all immunization event groups (and, in an RSP, comes before the Forecast group), or decide that order does not matter and say so.

message: SISC guidance Guidance on Detailed Message Structure and the Use of Specific LOINC Codes (Structure of the VXU (Z22) message): In narrative only. The guide describes both flavors as produced by a CDS engine and returned in RSP messages, and the Z22 co-constraint tables have no evaluation or forecast rows, so this holds in practice. It is not stated for the VXU.

section_title: Overall Structure of CDS in the RSP
message: SISC guidance Guidance on Detailed Message Structure and the Use of Specific LOINC Codes (Structure of the Z32 and Z42 messages; Table 4): Partly covered. The guide's CDS rules match for any RSP with CDS content (evaluation in each history group, exactly one Forecast group, placed last), and the Forecast section requires a shared OBX-4 per set. But the guide has no summary of which flavors each profile uses, and does not say whether a Z32 may carry evaluation or a forecast. Figure 20 is organized by flavor, not by profile.
recommendation: Add a short table like this guidance's Table 4 to section 4.4.4: each flavor against Z22, Z32, and Z42, with its cardinality.

message: SISC guidance Guidance on Detailed Message Structure and the Use of Specific LOINC Codes (Structure of the VXU (Z22) message; Z32; Z42): Reworded. The guide uses OBX-4 for the same purposes, but for VIS it says submitting systems SHOULD populate OBX-4 and IIS SHOULD use it when present, which is weaker than "must".
recommendation: Confirm that SHOULD for VIS linking is intended, since the guidance (and Release 1.5) required it.

message: SISC guidance Guidance on Detailed Message Structure and the Use of Specific LOINC Codes (Structure of the Z32 and Z42 messages (evaluation)): Conflict. The vaccine type comes first in the guide too. But the guide says dose validity SHALL be omitted when it cannot be determined, where this guidance (and the CDS in RSP TAB, and IGAMT) require it. This is already a finding from the TAB comparison (tab-cds-08).
recommendation: Resolve with tab-cds-08.

message: SISC guidance Guidance on Detailed Message Structure and the Use of Specific LOINC Codes (Structure of the Z32 and Z42 messages (forecast)): Reworded. The guide follows the CDS in RSP TAB, which replaced these rules. One change: the reason for recommendation is now MAY, even when a series is contraindicated or not recommended. The TAB comparison found the guide matches the TAB (tab-cds-17).
recommendation: Record in the change history that the reason for recommendation is no longer required.

message: SISC guidance Guidance on Detailed Message Structure and the Use of Specific LOINC Codes (Tables 1-3 (OBX-2)): Reworded. The guide accepts both CE and CWE and says IIS SHOULD use CE in responses; IGAMT fixes coded observations to 'CE' (except 75323-6, which is 'CWE'). Dates, counts, and dose validity match, and the DT_D flavor is kept. The CE/CWE inconsistency is already a finding (qf-igamt-c27-c28-ce-cwe).

SISC guidance Guidance on Detailed Message Structure and the Use of Specific LOINC Codes (Tables 1-3 (48767-8)): Conflict. IGAMT has 'CE' in the Z22 tables and 'ST' in the Z32 tables. Already a finding (qf-igamt-c27-c28-ce-cwe), which recommends a text type. This guidance supports 'TX'.
recommendation: Use 'TX' (or another text type) for 48767-8 in every profile, as this guidance did.

message: SISC guidance Guidance on Detailed Message Structure and the Use of Specific LOINC Codes (Tables 1-3 (value sets)): Partly covered. The other bindings match IGAMT. IGAMT binds 59784-9 to PHVS_HistoryOfDisease_IIS, a different name; check that it is the same PHIN VADS value set. 75323-6 still has no value set in IGAMT or the narrative. 30982-3 is 'ST' only in IGAMT. 59783-1 now uses LOINC answer codes, following the CDS in RSP TAB.
recommendation: Confirm the 59784-9 value set name, and bind 75323-6 to a value set (or say in the narrative that it is locally defined).

message: SISC guidance Guidance on Populating OBX-14 (Out of Scope): Partly covered. The guide covers the related-date codes, but not the advice to agree OBX-14's meaning with trading partners for other observations.
recommendation: Add a sentence that the meaning of OBX-14 for other observations is agreed between trading partners.

message: SISC guidance Guidance on Indicating Preferable and Contraindicated Vaccines (Structure of the Z42 message): Partly covered. The guide has the first rule ("SHOULD NOT be used ... when any vaccine in the group would be equally appropriate"). It does not say to skip it when only one product exists, or that the recommendation's dates apply to every preferred vaccine.
recommendation: Add the other two points to s1 or the narrative.

message: SISC guidance Guidance on Indicating Preferable and Contraindicated Vaccines (Structure of the Z42 message (OBX-5)): Reworded. The guide requires CVX (SHALL), which rules out the NDCs this guidance allowed. One vaccine per segment follows from the guide's "MAY be repeated" wording.
recommendation: Confirm that excluding NDC is intended, and record it in the change history if so.

message: SISC guidance Query Responses and Patient Protection (Guidance when implementing Release 1.5): In narrative only. The guide leaves consent enforcement to each IIS ("IIS are responsible for enforcing their own consent rules based on local authority") and uses a Z33 only when a record "cannot be disclosed". A normal Z32 or Z42 for a protected patient whose data may be shared follows from that, but is not said.

section_title: Z33 - Return a Response with No Person Records
message: SISC guidance Guidance for HL7 RSP Messages to Support Interoperability (Caveats; Summary): Partly covered. The IGAMT RSP profiles allow ERR [0..1], as the base standard requires, so the limit is enforced. The narrative never mentions it, or says which error to return when there are several. Readers who know the ACK (which allows many ERR segments) will not expect the difference.
recommendation: Add a sentence to the RSP profile sections: an RSP carries at most one ERR segment, so the IIS returns the most significant issue.

message: SISC guidance Guidance for HL7 RSP Messages to Support Interoperability (Query Response Guidance (query is successfully processed)): In narrative only. The guide describes the response profiles as the "controlled set of outcomes" of matching, and its Z33 section says that a Z33 means the IIS "has processed the query". It does not say outright that finding no patient, or several, is a successful query rather than an error.

SISC guidance Guidance for HL7 RSP Messages to Support Interoperability (Summary (Table 2)): Partly covered. The guide matches the profiles to these outcomes (figure 17 and the Z32, Z42, and Z33 sections) but does not give the QAK-2 values ('OK' and 'NF').
recommendation: Include the QAK-2 values when this is covered (see sisc-rsp-09).

section_title: Z31 - Return a List of Candidates
message: SISC guidance Guidance for HL7 RSP Messages to Support Interoperability (Summary (Table 2)): Conflict. The guide lets a Z31 answer a Z44 query as well, following the Query Response Flexibility TAB (January 2024), which replaced this part of the guidance. This change is intended. The IGAMT Z31 profile still requires QPD-1 'Z34', a conflict recorded in the TAB comparison (tab-qrf-04). The guide also does not give the QAK-2 value for a Z31 ('OK').
recommendation: Record in the change history that a Z31 may now answer a Z44 query, replacing this guidance, and give the QAK-2 value for a Z31.
