TA question (MSH Message Header, MSH-15 / MSH-16 Accept and Application Acknowledgment Type): Partly answers. IGAMT fixes MSH-15 to 'NE' and MSH-16 to 'AL', but the narrative never explains acknowledgement modes. 3.3.2 has an intermediary return 'CR' (a commit acknowledgement), which the sender's MSH-15 'NE' says it does not want.
recommendation: Explain in the ACK profile that MSH-15 'NE' and MSH-16 'AL' mean one application acknowledgement and no commit acknowledgement, and square that with the 'CR' an intermediary may return.

message: TA question (MSH Message Header, MSH-21 Message Profile Identifier): Differs. Asked in 2019 and 2020 and answered: return a Z33 RSP, not a Z23. The guide now says a query that cannot be processed (malformed MSH or QPD, missing required header information) gets a Z23 ACK, and IGAMT allows MSH-9.2 'Q11' in the Z23 profile. Systems built to the past answer will send and expect Z33.
recommendation: Confirm the change, record it in the change history, and say which query errors get a Z23 ACK and which a Z33 RSP (for example, an invalid QPD parameter). Z23 is also listed under the RSP profiles, though it is an ACK; say so.

message: TA question (MSH Message Header, MSH-10 Message Control ID): Gap. MSH-10 is required, but the guide never says it must be unique (the past answer says per sender, at least per day) or that MSA-2 echoes it. The query tag in QPD-2 is not discussed either.
recommendation: In a Message Header section, say MSH-10 SHALL be unique for the sender and is echoed in MSA-2.

message: TA question (MSH Message Header, MSH-6 Receiving Facility): Gap. The guide says nothing about MSH-3, MSH-5 or MSH-6 values: that they are agreed between trading partners, that an IIS should require specific values only when it needs them for routing, or which party to name when an HIE passes a message through. TA has answered this the same way several times.
recommendation: Add a short Message Header section to chapter 2 covering MSH-3, MSH-5, MSH-6 and MSH-23: agreed during onboarding, required by an IIS only when needed for routing or processing, not changed by intermediaries, and in an ACK or RSP normally echoing the sender's MSH-3 and MSH-4.

message: TA question (MSH Message Header, MSH-9 Message Type): Partly answers. The MSA-1 guidance says 'AR' was "previously" used for an unsupported message type, event code or processing ID, and removes only the fourth reason. It never says, in the present tense, that these conditions still get 'AR', or that "message type" covers all of MSH-9 (code, trigger event, structure). AIRA promised this clarification in 2024.
recommendation: Add a statement: an IIS SHALL return 'AR' when any component of MSH-9, MSH-11 or MSH-12 is not supported, with an ERR segment naming the field.

message: TA question (MSH Message Header, MSH-22 Sending Responsible Organization): Partly answers. The guide ties transport credentials to MSH-4 and says authorization to submit for another organization is set up at onboarding. It does not say whether an IIS should check MSH-22 against that authorization, or what severity to give a mismatch.
recommendation: Add a statement on MSH-22 that is not authorized for the submitting organization: for example, IIS MAY validate it against onboarding records, and report a mismatch as an Error or Warning by local policy.

message: TA question (MSH Message Header, MSH-4 Sending Facility): Differs. The 2017 answer said an IIS need not require MSH-4 on queries if it does not use it. The guide now makes MSH-4 required (R) and says query messages SHALL include it. A deliberate change.

TA question (MSH Message Header, MSH-7 Date/Time of Message): Partly answers. 2.8.1 says consistent precision is required, but not what precision is allowed or that a receiver must accept fractional seconds.
recommendation: State that receivers SHALL accept any precision the DTM data type allows, down to fractions of a second.

message: TA question (MSH Message Header, MSH-4 Sending Facility): Partly answers. The guide mentions OID-based identifiers only as a possible future use, and leaves assigning authorities to each IIS. There is no general guidance on when to use OIDs.

TA question (MSH Message Header, MSH-4 Sending Facility): Partly answers. Section 2.7.1 says HD.1 carries the organization identifier and the other HD components are optional. It does not say they must not carry a second identifier (past answer: move it to MSH-22 or the WSDL Facility ID).
recommendation: Say that HD.2 and HD.3 qualify the identifier in HD.1 (its namespace) and are not for additional identifiers.

message: TA question (MSH Message Header, MSH-3 Sending Application): Gap. The SFT segment is optional in every profile, but the narrative never mentions it, so there is no guidance on where to identify the sending software.
recommendation: Add a sentence to a Message Header section that SFT identifies the sending software and its version, and that MSH-3 identifies the application, not its version.

message: TA question (MSH Message Header, MSH-4 Sending Facility): Differs. The guide answers how to represent several facilities: MSH-4 is the submitting organization operating the interface, and child facilities go in RXA-11.4 or ORC-17. The 2022 answer suggested copying RXA-11.4 into MSH-4, which the guide no longer allows.

TA question (MSH Message Header, MSH-7 Date/Time of Message): Gap. The 2020 answer said not to accept messages dated far in the past. The guide says MSH-7 is not for clinical use but not whether an IIS may check it for plausibility, and 3.3.5 s2 discourages rejecting for minor conformance issues.
recommendation: Say whether an implausible MSH-7 (far past or future) is an Error, a Warning, or ignored.

message: TA question (MSH Message Header, MSH-10 Message Control ID): Gap. The guide requires one ACK for every VXU and has IIS deduplicate records, but says nothing about a message received twice (same MSH-10 and content): whether the IIS may reject it, and with what severity.
recommendation: Say how an IIS acknowledges a duplicate message (accept and deduplicate, or reject with a Warning).

message: TA question (MSH Message Header, MSH-5 Receiving Application): Partly answers. MSH-5 and MSH-6 are RE in IGAMT, and the guide says intermediaries must be transparent. It does not say who defines their values, whether an IIS may reject a message when they are empty, or that the IZ Gateway does not change them (the IZ Gateway is out of scope).

TA question (MSH Message Header, MSH-23 Receiving Responsible Organization): Partly answers. The IGAMT binding answers the identifier type question (HL70203). The narrative never mentions MSH-23, and 2.7.1 says the components after HD.1 are optional. The past advice not to require MSH-22 components 6 to 10 is not in the guide.

TA question (MSH Message Header, MSH-11 Processing ID): Partly answers. MSH-11 is required and bound to HL70103, and the MSA-1 guidance mentions an unsupported processing ID. The guide does not say what an IIS does with 'T' or 'D' arriving at a production endpoint.
recommendation: State that production interfaces SHALL send 'P', and how an IIS treats other values (see ta-q33-020).

message: TA question (MSH Message Header, MSH-21 Message Profile Identifier): Differs. The 2024 answer: run the query anyway with a Warning, or reject with a Z33 RSP (MSA-1 'AE', ERR on MSH-21). Under the guide, missing required header information gets a Z23 ACK, and 'AE' no longer means rejected. See ta-q03-107.

section_title: Focus on Data Quality and Program Goals
message: TA question (MSH Message Header, MSH-3 Sending Application): By appeal. IGAMT gives no length for MSH-3, and the guide says not to enforce arbitrary rules or reject for minor conformance preferences. But it never says what the lengths that IGAMT does carry (MSH-8 up to 40, MSH-10 up to 199) mean, or that base-standard lengths are not normative.
recommendation: In 5.11 (compatibility with the base standard) or 4.1, say what a length in the profiles means, and that IIS should not reject a value only because it is longer than a base-standard length.

message: TAB Acknowledgment (ACK) Messaging: Updated Specifications and Guidance (ERR-5 Values): Missing. The narrative refers to "a national code set" but never names it, links to it, or includes it. The guide's own SHALL, SHOULD, and MAY (implement High, Medium, and Low priority codes) cannot be followed without it, because the narrative does not say which codes have which priority. The value set bound to ERR-5 in chapter 7 (HL70533_IZ01) is the 2017 code list plus 5044 and has no priorities. This site now shows the set (version 2026-07-06, pending publication by AIRA) as Appendix D, linked from 3.3.3.4; the narrative still needs to name and cite it.
recommendation: Name and cite the national set in 3.3.3.4 and Resources (once AIRA posts it), and carry Appendix D, the codes with their priorities, into the guide.

message: TAB Acknowledgment (ACK) Messaging: Updated Specifications and Guidance (ERR-5 Specifications): Conflict. The narrative matches the TAB, but the profiles do not allow it. HL70533_IZ01 is marked closed and has 67 codes (1-7, 2000-2701, and 5044). The national set (Appendix D) has 280: 213 of them, including 16 of the 20 High priority codes (such as 2018, vaccination date before birth, and 3019, date of birth missing), are not in the value set, so an IIS that meets the SHALL sends ERR-5 values the profile does not allow. The value set also still lists 2202, 2203, and 2502, which the national set has deprecated.
recommendation: Update HL70533_IZ01 in IGAMT to the national set (or make it open and point to the national set), and record the version of the set that the guide adopts.

section_title: Dose Validity and Reason for Validity
message: TAB CDS in RSP Alignment (Table 2: 59781-5 Dose validity): Conflict. The guide says "If dose validity cannot be determined or is unavailable at query time, the dose-validity OBX ... SHALL be omitted" (stated twice, in 4.7.7.4 s3 and in 4.7.7.1 "Future work" s2). The TAB requires dose validity for every evaluation, and so does IGAMT (59781-5 is R in the Z42 evaluation group). The Y/N rule matches; the order after the vaccine type is in narrative only.
recommendation: Remove the omission rule (both copies), or take it to SISC as a change to the TAB and to IGAMT. Move the two statements in "Future work" (4.7.7.1) to the sections they belong to; that card is otherwise about future guidance.

message: TAB CDS in RSP Alignment (Table 3: 30979-9 Vaccines due next): Conflict. The guide says "If needed to support legacy systems, IIS SHOULD include the legacy LOINC 30979-9 (Vaccines Due Next) after LOINC 30956-7", the opposite of the TAB. IGAMT agrees with the TAB: 30979-9 is not in the Z42 forecast co-constraints, so a message that includes it does not conform.
recommendation: Replace s3 with "IIS SHOULD NOT return LOINC 30979-9 (Vaccines Due Next)."

section_title: Z31 - Return a List of Candidates
message: TAB Query Response Flexibility: Z31 Response for Z34 and Z44 Queries (Z31 compared with IGAMT): Conflict. The IGAMT Z31 profile has IZ-67a ("QPD-1.1 shall contain the value 'Z34'") and IZ-67b (QPD-1.2 "Request Immunization History"). The RSP echoes the query's QPD, so a Z31 answering a Z44 fails validation. The Z33 profile already allows either query (IZ-71a and IZ-71b).
recommendation: Replace IZ-67a and IZ-67b in the Z31 profile with the Z34-or-Z44 constraints used in Z33 (IZ-71a, IZ-71b).

message: TAB Returning IIS Patient Immunization Record Information in a Z32 and Z42 RSP (Table 1: Immunization types (refused)): Conflict. The guide says "IIS SHOULD NOT return refusal records in query (RSP) responses" and "Querying systems SHALL NOT expect refusals to be returned", because refusals "have no role in clinical query/response exchanges". The TAB says the opposite. (The CDS in RSP Alignment TAB also lists refusals among the non-CDS order groups that follow the history.)
recommendation: CDC and SISC decide. If the guide's position stands, it changes a published TAB and should say so; otherwise change 4.8.7.4 to the TAB's SHOULD.

message: TAB Returning IIS Patient Immunization Record Information in a Z32 and Z42 RSP (Tables 2 and 3 compared with IGAMT): Conflict. The IGAMT Z32 and Z42 profiles still have the usages the TAB replaced (its "National IG Usage" columns). Z32: PD1 and NK1 RE (TAB O); PID-6, PID-10, PID-13, PID-22 RE (TAB O, PID-6 SHOULD NOT); PID-11 RE in both (TAB O); RXA-9 R for CP/PA (TAB O; see also qf-igamt-rxa9-rsp); RXA-20 RE (TAB R); RXA-21 O (TAB R, 'A'); RXA-10 and RXA-15 to RXA-17 and ORC-12 conditional on RXA-9 = '00' (TAB RE for CP/PA, X otherwise). Z42 has no PD1 or NK1 at all, and the same RXA differences.
recommendation: Apply Tables 2 and 3 to PID_IZ01/IZ02, RXA_IZ02/IZ03, ORC_IZ01/IZ02, and the Z32 and Z42 message structures.

section_title: Reporting Immunizations: Single vs. Multiple Administered Vaccinations per VXU
message: TAB Scenarios for Updates and Queries (Executive Summary; Table 1: Vaccination administered during an encounter): Conflict. The guide says a submitting system SHALL support at least one approach and "MAY support both approaches if operationally required". The TAB says SHALL NOT support both.
recommendation: CDC and SISC decide. If the guide's MAY stands, it changes a published TAB and should say so; otherwise change s2 to "A submitting system SHALL NOT support both approaches."

section_title: IIS Core Intent and Message Disposition
message: TAB Acknowledgment (ACK) Messaging: Updated Specifications and Guidance (Summary: What Can Be Inferred from the ACK? (Key Takeaways)): Partly covered. The guide says rejection does not imply that nothing was stored (s4), and that resubmission means a corrected message. It never says the whole message is resent, or that submitters should not try to work out what was stored, which is the practical consequence the TAB draws from s4.
recommendation: Add to 3.3.1: "After a rejection, the submitting system SHALL correct and resubmit the complete message and SHALL NOT attempt to determine which parts of it were stored."

message: TAB Acknowledgment (ACK) Messaging: Updated Specifications and Guidance (MSA-1 Specifications (Table 3)): Partly covered. All of it is there, and figure 13 matches Table 3, but the statements lost their subject in conversion: s1 reads "SHALL be returned to indicate VXU acceptance..." and s2 "SHALL be returned when the ERR-4 severity is 'W'..." without saying which MSA-1 value. The three other rules (AA SHALL NOT, AE SHALL NOT, AR SHALL) are left in the narrative and are not numbered statements.
recommendation: Write the five rules as five complete statements ("MSA-1 SHALL be 'AA' when...", and so on). The Word draft nests them under the MSA-1 value; check the conversion of that list too.

message: TAB Acknowledgment (ACK) Messaging: Updated Specifications and Guidance (ERR-5 Values (code ranges)): Partly covered. The guide lists the categories in a sentence, without their number ranges, leaves out "processing results" (5000-5999) ("among others"), and does not say to use the legacy codes 1-7 only when no more specific code exists.
recommendation: Give the ranges as a table in 3.3.3.4, including 5000-5999 and the rule for codes 1-7.

section_title: IIS Core Intent and Message Disposition
message: TAB Acknowledgment (ACK) Messaging: Updated Specifications and Guidance (Appendix B: Core intent and acknowledgment messaging examples (Table 7)): Missing. The guide has the address example but not this table, which is the clearest illustration of where core intent draws the line. The ACK examples in appendix A show AA, AE, and AR messages but not these scenarios.
recommendation: Add Table 7 to 3.3.1, or as example messages linked from it.

section_title: Z42 - Return Evaluated Immunization History and Forecast
message: TAB CDS in RSP Alignment (Scope (footnote 1); RSP Example): Partly covered. The Z42 section says the response includes evaluation and forecast results, but no statement requires them, and nothing says a Z32 may carry them or that section 4.7 then applies. The IGAMT Z32 profile does allow a forecast group.
recommendation: Add to 4.7: "A Z42 response SHALL include evaluation and forecast information. A Z32 response MAY include it; when it does, the requirements of this section apply."

message: TAB CDS in RSP Alignment (Forecast observations): Partly covered. Single group, one forecast per series, and OBX-4 linking are statements. The ORC/RXA values are described only for patient-level groups in general (4.4.1), which says RXA-3 "can be populated with the current date but does not convey clinical timing". The TAB requires RXA-3 to be the date of the forecast.
recommendation: Add to 4.7.8.1 the TAB's rule for the forecast ORC/RXA: RXA-3 the forecast date, RXA-5.1 '998', RXA-20 'NA'.

message: TAB CDS in RSP Alignment (Table 3: 30956-7 Vaccine type): Partly covered. The guide does not say that each forecast's vaccine type CVX must be unique within the forecast group.
recommendation: Add "The CVX in the vaccine type OBX SHALL be unique among the forecasts in the forecast order group."

message: TAB CDS in RSP Alignment (Table 3: 38890-0 Component vaccine type): Partly covered. The guide only forbids using 38890-0 "to initiate a forecast", which reads as allowing it later in the forecast group. The TAB forbids it anywhere in the forecast, as does IGAMT (not in the forecast co-constraints).
recommendation: "LOINC 38890-0 (Component Vaccine Type) SHALL NOT be returned in the forecast order group."

message: TAB CDS in RSP Alignment (Status in immunization series (concepts)): Partly covered. The guide requires only that the status distinguish "complete" from "another dose due". It does not require On schedule as such, and does not mention Overdue or Too old as SHOULD.
recommendation: State the TAB's concept levels: SHALL Complete and On schedule; SHOULD Overdue and Too old; MAY others.

message: TAB CDS in RSP Alignment (Status in immunization series (local codes); Table 4): Missing. Neither the documentation requirement nor Table 4 is in the narrative; the guide points to the chapter 7 co-constraint table for the answer codes. The codes are in an IGAMT value set, but without the TAB's usage (R or P) for each.
recommendation: Add the local-code documentation SHALL to 4.7.8.3, and Table 4 (or a link to the value set with each code's usage).

message: TAB Submission of Self-Administered FluMist Vaccine to IIS (Background; RXA-9 and RXA-10): Missing. The guide does not mention self- or caregiver-administered vaccines. Its rule that "Administered vaccinations SHALL represent doses given directly by the reporting organization" does not fit a dose the pharmacy dispensed and the patient gave, and a reader could conclude these doses must be reported as historical. IGAMT accepts the TAB's values (RXA-10 is RE with XCN_IZ01; 'MR' is R in HL70203_IZ01).
recommendation: Decide how self- and caregiver-administered doses are reported in general, then add it to 4.6.1: for example, "A dose dispensed by the reporting organization and administered by the patient or a caregiver is reported as administered (RXA-9 '00'), with the patient or caregiver in RXA-10." Note that CVX 333 already identifies the self- or caregiver-administered product.

message: TAB Messaging Non-patient Person Names in HL7 (Scope (Table 1)): Conflict. The guide's list has "ORC-1 Entered By". ORC-1 is the Order Control code; Entered By is ORC-10. The other four fields are right. The guide does not say which message types each field applies to.
recommendation: Change "ORC-1" to "ORC-10", and add the TAB's Table 1 (field by VXU, QBP, RSP).

message: TAB About Technical Advisory Bulletins (Overview; relationship to the National IG): Missing. Section 6.2 describes TABs in general and says their content "is incorporated into future versions", but not what that means for this release. A reader cannot tell which published TABs this guide incorporates, whether those TABs still apply after it is published (for example, to systems still on Release 1.5), which document wins where they differ (this comparison found several conflicts), or that new TABs will build on this guide.
recommendation: Add a card to 6.2, after 6.2.5, along these lines: "This guide incorporates the TABs published through [month year], listed in [appendix]. For systems implementing this guide, it replaces those TABs; where a TAB and this guide differ, this guide applies [and the difference is listed]. The TABs remain in effect for systems still implementing Release 1.5. TABs published after this guide build on it, and are incorporated into the next release." CDC and SISC decide the supersession rule and the cut-off date.

message: TAB About Technical Advisory Bulletins (Value set specifications (Table 2)): Missing. The guide defines element usage (R, RE, C, O, X) and value set extensibility, but not code usage within a value set. IGAMT gives code usage throughout (for example ASN as E in HL70201_IZ01), and the Phone and Email TAB relies on it.
recommendation: Add the TAB's Table 2 to 4.3 (Dynamic and Fixed Code Sets), and say that the value set tables give code usage.

message: TAB Messaging Phone and Email; Telecommunication Use Code and Equipment Type Values (Executive Summary; PID-13 Field Definition (Table 2)): Partly covered. The guide's statements cover PID-13 only (s2: "The first repetition of PID-13 SHALL represent the primary contact number"). The narrative mentions NK1-5; QPD-9 is not mentioned anywhere in 4.5.4.
recommendation: Make s2 and s4 apply to PID-13, NK1-5, and QPD-9.

message: TAB Messaging Phone and Email; Telecommunication Use Code and Equipment Type Values (PID-13 Field Definition (Table 2, clarification)): Conflict. The guide says "Systems SHALL send patient contact information in PID-13 and guardian or next-of-kin contact information in NK1-5", which reads as keeping a guardian's number out of PID-13. Its narrative (a newborn's number may belong to a parent) and s5 agree with the TAB, so the statement is the problem.
recommendation: Reword s1: "PID-13 SHALL carry the contact information used to reach the patient, which for a minor may be a guardian's. Next-of-kin and guardian contact information SHALL be sent in NK1-5."

message: TAB Messaging Phone and Email; Telecommunication Use Code and Equipment Type Values (QPD-9 compared with IGAMT): Conflict. In IGAMT, QPD-9 (Patient Home Phone) is 0..1 in the Z34 and Z44 queries, so a query cannot carry a phone number and an email. The TAB's rule cannot be followed for QPD-9 as profiled.
recommendation: Decide whether QPD-9 should repeat (an IGAMT change) or whether a query carries only the primary phone, and say so in 4.5.4.

message: TAB Messaging Phone and Email; Telecommunication Use Code and Equipment Type Values (Table 3 compared with the IGAMT value set): Conflict. HL70201_IZ01 marks ASN as E (not allowed), so a message using it does not conform, although the TAB and the guide (s3) allow it. The other codes match.
recommendation: Change ASN to P in HL70201_IZ01.

message: TAB Patient Name (PID-5) Updates to Support Patient Matching (Name type code (HL70200) Value Set usage for PID-5 (Table 1)): Conflict. The guide says "Systems SHOULD NOT send names with ambiguous or administrative meaning such as Business, Partner/Spouse, or Licensing names", a SHOULD NOT where the TAB says SHALL NOT, and it does not mention Father's name or the SHOULD NOT codes.
recommendation: Replace s3 with the TAB's two lists: SHOULD NOT NAV, TEMP, BAD, D; SHALL NOT F, I, K, P. Better, add Table 1 to 4.5.2.1.

message: TAB Patient Name (PID-5) Updates to Support Patient Matching (Table 1 compared with the IGAMT value set): Conflict. HL70200_IZ01 (closed) does not include REL, MSK, or NOUSE, which the TAB allows (MAY), so they cannot be sent. It allows D (P), which the TAB says SHOULD NOT be supported, and leaves out NAV, TEMP, BAD, F, and K. It also has R and S (both E), which are not in the TAB's table.
recommendation: Align HL70200_IZ01 with Table 1, including its usage for each code.

message: TAB Patient Name (PID-5) Updates to Support Patient Matching (Data type specifications by name type code (Table 2)): Partly covered. The guide describes this in narrative ("official registry and newborn names must contain both a family and given name, while other types ... may have only one component") and says two flavors "will be defined", but this is the guide that was to define them. There is no statement, no component table, and no flavor names. In IGAMT, the two XPN flavors exist but are applied by slicing the whole PID segment, so 'NB' names are not held to the family-and-given rule (see the IGAMT review, qf-igamt-c36-name-flavors).
recommendation: Name the flavors (XPN_IZ01, XPN_IZ02), add Table 2 and a SHALL statement to 4.5.2.5, and resolve the IGAMT slicing finding so the rule applies per repetition.

message: TAB Patient Name (PID-5) Updates to Support Patient Matching (Name requirements (IIS validation)): Conflict. The guide says "IIS SHALL NOT rely on textual pattern detection (e.g., "Baby Boy") to infer that a record represents a newborn", which rules out the placeholder check the TAB allows (and that the national ERR-5 code 2201, Invalid Name (Baby), exists for). The IIS's SHALL to offer an alternate process when an accurate name is rejected is not in the guide.
recommendation: Narrow 4.5.2.6 s3 to "IIS SHALL NOT treat a name as a newborn placeholder only because of its text when it is submitted with name type 'L'", or remove it; and add the TAB's alternate-process SHALL to 4.5.2.12 or 4.5.2.10.

section_title: Z31 - Return a List of Candidates
message: TAB Query Response Flexibility: Z31 Response for Z34 and Z44 Queries (SHALL requirements): Missing. The guide tells querying systems how to re-query after a user selects a candidate, but does not require them to accept a Z31 for a Z44 query. A system built to the earlier guide, where a Z44 could not get a Z31, may not.
recommendation: Add to 3.5.2.3: "Querying systems SHALL be prepared to receive a Z31 response to either a Z34 or a Z44 query."

message: TAB Additional "Unknown" Race and Ethnicity Codes (Tables 1 and 2 (submitting system conformance)): Conflict. The guide says sending systems "SHOULD select and consistently implement either ASKU or PHC1175 ... but not both", a SHOULD where the TAB has SHALL NOT.
recommendation: "Sending systems SHALL NOT send both ASKU and PHC1175 to the same receiving system; they SHALL choose one."

message: TAB Additional "Unknown" Race and Ethnicity Codes (Additional "unknown" race and ethnic group codes): Conflict. The guide does not say which coding system the three codes use. IGAMT gives them as NULLFL (UNK, ASKU, and, for ethnicity, PHC1175) and CDCPHINVS (PHC1175 for race), so the TAB's own examples carry a coding system the profiles do not list. The value sets are open, so a validator would probably warn rather than fail.
recommendation: Decide which coding system identifier these codes carry (the TAB says CDCREC), state it in 4.5.5.2, and make the IGAMT value sets match.

message: TAB Additional "Unknown" Race and Ethnicity Codes (Processing a VXU with an unknown patient race and/or ethnic group): Partly covered. The guide says IIS must accommodate unknown and refused responses "without rejecting valid immunization messages", and must not reject the three unknown codes, but has no statement for a code the IIS does not recognize (an invalid code).
recommendation: Add to 4.5.5.1: "Except where prohibited by law or policy, IIS SHALL process a VXU with or without valid race and ethnicity codes; an unrecognized code is reported in the ACK and the field treated as not valued."

message: TAB Returning IIS Patient Immunization Record Information in a Z32 and Z42 RSP (Table 1: Immunization types (deleted)): Missing. The guide does not say that deleted immunizations are excluded from a response.
recommendation: Add "IIS SHALL NOT return deleted immunizations" to 4.6.2.6 or 3.5.2.

section_title: Use of Immunity Information in Forecasting
message: TAB Returning IIS Patient Immunization Record Information in a Z32 and Z42 RSP (Table 1: Observations associated with a patient): Partly covered. The guide says IIS that use immunity information for recommendations SHOULD return it, which is narrower than the TAB, and has no statement about returning contraindications. It makes returning patient-level reactions a SHOULD where the TAB says MAY.
recommendation: Add the TAB's SHOULD for contraindications and both immunity observations to 3.5.2 or 4.8.

section_title: Use of Administered vs. Historical on Output
message: TAB Returning IIS Patient Immunization Record Information in a Z32 and Z42 RSP (Table 3: RXA-9, RXA-20, RXA-21): Partly covered. RXA-9 is covered (the guide prefers it empty in responses, which the TAB allows). Nothing says RXA-20 and RXA-21 are required in responses, or that RXA-21 is 'A'.
recommendation: Add to 4.6.2.6: "In an RSP, RXA-20 SHALL be populated, and RXA-21 SHALL be 'A'."

message: TAB Returning IIS Patient Immunization Record Information in a Z32 and Z42 RSP (Table 3: vaccination event fields): Missing. The guide does not say which vaccination event details are returned, or that they are left out for other completion statuses.
recommendation: Add the TAB's rule to 4.6.2.6.

message: TAB System Entry Date/Time (RXA-22) Definition (Executive Summary; Table 1: RXA-22 definition): Missing. RXA-22 is not mentioned anywhere in the guide, and IGAMT has no definition for it. A submitter reading the HL7 base standard would send the first entry date, and an update would carry the same value as the original add.
recommendation: Add the TAB's definition to 4.6 (Immunization Information), for example in 4.6.4 next to updates: "For administered and historical immunizations, RXA-22 is the most recent date and time the immunization information was entered or updated in the submitting system." List it in 5.11.3 (Reinterpretation of Base Standard Semantics), since it differs from the base definition.

section_title: Types of Information Carried in a VXU
message: TAB Scenarios for Updates and Queries (Table 1: Evidence of immunity, adverse reaction, contraindication, refusal or exemption): Partly covered. The guide allows sending each of these (MAY statements in 3.2.2 and 4.8), and says IIS MAY ignore them and SHOULD keep processing the rest of the message, so a submitter cannot tell from the ACK whether they were used. It has no statement that these recordings may trigger a VXU on their own, and none requiring coordination with the IIS before sending them (only for locally extended codes).
recommendation: Add to 3.2.5: "Recording evidence of immunity, an adverse reaction, a contraindication, or a refusal MAY trigger a VXU, or the information MAY be sent with other vaccination information. Submitting systems SHALL coordinate with the IIS to confirm that it supports this information."

message: TAB Scenarios for Updates and Queries (Table 2: Patient or guardian portal): Reworded. The trigger and re-query statements match. The limits are weakened: "Jurisdictions and implementers SHOULD agree on reasonable daily limits and controls to prevent over-querying", where the TAB has three SHALLs for portals.
recommendation: Replace s3 with: "For patient or guardian portal queries, systems SHALL limit the number of queries per patient per day, SHALL coordinate the limit with the IIS, and SHALL have controls to prevent over-querying."

message: TAB Acknowledgment (ACK) Messaging: Updated Specifications and Guidance (Transport-Level Failures): Covered. The guide's list leaves out "SOAP message too large" and puts "Other routing/connectivity issue" on the same line as the SOAP item, which looks like a conversion artifact of a nested list.

TAB Acknowledgment (ACK) Messaging: Updated Specifications and Guidance (Executive Summary; MSA-1 Guidance): In narrative only. The guide explains that this reason is removed, but has no conformance statement for it. The TAB states it as a SHALL NOT in its executive summary.
recommendation: Add a statement to 3.3.4.1 MSA-1 Guidance.

section_title: IIS Core Intent and Message Disposition
message: TAB Acknowledgment (ACK) Messaging: Updated Specifications and Guidance (Acceptance and Processing Terms: IIS Core Intent): Reworded. The guide's narrative repeats the TAB's definition, but its statements define acceptance and rejection through "Critical Data", a term the TAB does not use: accepted when the patient is associated "and all submitted Critical Data is processed and stored". The two agree if Critical Data means the patient's identity plus each submitted vaccination; the TAB's examples (one of three immunizations stored: reject; TB result not stored: accept) fit that reading. Because Critical Data is otherwise left to local policy (see tab-ack-g03), the statements can be read more broadly than the TAB.
recommendation: Confirm that Critical Data is meant to equal the TAB's core intent, and say so in the Critical Data key term, or phrase s1 and s2 in the TAB's terms (patient associated or created, each submitted vaccination recorded).

message: TAB Acknowledgment (ACK) Messaging: Updated Specifications and Guidance (Successful, Qualified Successful, and Unsuccessful Transmissions): Partly covered. The guide uses "qualified successful" and "unsuccessful" in 3.3.4 and 3.3.4.1 but never defines the three terms. Key Terms (1.3) define Core Intent and Rejection, but not Accept or these three outcomes.
recommendation: Add Successful, Qualified Successful, and Unsuccessful to Key Terms, or define them in 3.3.1.

message: TAB Acknowledgment (ACK) Messaging: Updated Specifications and Guidance (ERR-2 Specifications): In narrative only. The SHALL is in the narrative of 3.3.3.1, which has no numbered statements.
recommendation: Make it statement s1 of 3.3.3.1.

message: TAB Acknowledgment (ACK) Messaging: Updated Specifications and Guidance (ERR-2 Guidance): Reworded. The guide says "ERR-2 can reference only one location per segment". "Per segment" can be read as one location per message segment involved, which is not what the TAB means (one location per ERR segment).
recommendation: Say "only one location per ERR segment", or drop "per segment".

message: TAB Acknowledgment (ACK) Messaging: Updated Specifications and Guidance (ACK Integration into Submitting and Receiving Systems): In narrative only. The SHALL is in the narrative of 3.3.3.3 and is not a numbered statement. The HIMSS white paper is cited [6] in 3.3.5, not here.
recommendation: Make it a statement of 3.3.3.3, with the actor (submitting systems), and cite [6] there.

message: TAB Acknowledgment (ACK) Messaging: Updated Specifications and Guidance (ERR-5 Guidance: Extensibility and Coordination): Reworded. The guide says to coordinate with "the guide's maintaining organization" instead of naming AIRA, which maintains the code set.
recommendation: Name AIRA as the maintainer of the national ERR-5 code set and say how to request a code.

message: TAB Acknowledgment (ACK) Messaging: Updated Specifications and Guidance (Not in the TAB): Guide adds. "An IIS SHALL generate exactly one application-level ACK in response to each successfully received VXU message." The TAB has no such requirement (section 2.5 says the same in prose).

TAB Acknowledgment (ACK) Messaging: Updated Specifications and Guidance (Not in the TAB): Guide adds. "ACK messages SHALL summarize the processing outcome of the submitted message, not intermediate workflow states." Not in the TAB.

section_title: IIS Core Intent and Message Disposition
message: TAB Acknowledgment (ACK) Messaging: Updated Specifications and Guidance (Not in the TAB): Guide adds. Critical Data, and "IIS MAY expand the definition of Critical Data through jurisdictional policy, provided that such expansion is documented in local messaging specifications". The TAB leaves the rules to local policy too, but does not define Critical Data or require local documentation (see tab-ack-06).

TAB Acknowledgment (ACK) Messaging: Updated Specifications and Guidance (Not in the TAB): Guide adds. "Each discrete issue ... SHALL be represented by a separate ERR segment" and "The absence of ERR segments with Warning or Error severity SHALL indicate that no corrective action is required." Both follow from the TAB but are not stated in it.

section_title: Use of ACKs in Interface Monitoring
message: TAB Acknowledgment (ACK) Messaging: Updated Specifications and Guidance (Not in the TAB): Guide adds. "IIS SHALL ensure that severities ... accurately reflect expected follow-up actions" and "Submitting systems SHALL analyze ACK feedback in aggregate to identify recurring data quality patterns." The TAB asks for issues to be conveyed in aggregate, but does not require submitters to analyze them.

TAB CDS in RSP Alignment (Organization requirements: Vaccination history/evaluation): In narrative only. The first two are covered by 4.7.5 s1. The combination-vaccine rule is described (Pediarix as three evaluated groups) but is not a conformance statement.
recommendation: Add to 4.7.7.2 "A combination vaccination evaluated for more than one vaccine group SHALL have a separate evaluated group for each."

section_title: Overall Structure of CDS in the RSP
message: TAB CDS in RSP Alignment (Organization requirements: Non-CDS Order Groups; Forecast): Reworded. The guide makes the position of the forecast group a SHALL (the TAB says SHOULD), and states the order of the non-CDS groups only in narrative and figure 30.
recommendation: Confirm that the guide means to raise the forecast position from SHOULD to SHALL.

message: TAB CDS in RSP Alignment (Evaluation observations): In narrative only. For forecasts, OBX-4 linking is a statement (4.7.8.1 s2). For evaluations, the guide says only that shared OBX-4 values group "related evaluation or recommendation observations" (4.4.2.4), with no SHALL.
recommendation: Add to 4.7.7: "The OBX segments of each evaluated group SHALL share an OBX-4 value."

message: TAB CDS in RSP Alignment (Table 2: 30956-7 Vaccine type; 38890-0 Component vaccine type): Covered. Covered, but these four statements sit under the second "Future work" heading (4.7.7.3) instead of 4.7.7.2, Vaccine Type and Component Identification, where they belong. Likewise the first "Future work" (4.7.7.1) holds two evaluation statements. Each "Future work" sub-heading in the Word draft has captured the statements of the section before or after it.
recommendation: Move the statements to 4.7.7.2 and 4.7.7.4 (or make "Future work" a paragraph rather than a heading), and keep a single "Future work" section.

section_title: Z42 - Return Evaluated Immunization History and Forecast
message: TAB CDS in RSP Alignment (RSP Example): Partly covered. The guide has a "History and Forecast" example, but not the TAB's teaching points (a vaccination with no evaluation, a combination vaccine evaluated twice, an invalid dose with its reason). The TAB's own example uses 59778-3 for Latest date, where its Table 3 (and the guide) has 59777-3; that is an error in the TAB, not the guide.
recommendation: Add the TAB's example (with 59777-3) to appendix A and link it from 4.7.

message: TAB Submission of Self-Administered FluMist Vaccine to IIS (Executive Summary; PID-11): In narrative only. The guide does not discuss how a national submitter decides which IIS to send to. That is a submitter's business rule and does not need a statement.

TAB Submission of Self-Administered FluMist Vaccine to IIS (Expected Interface Specifications): Partly covered. After this guide is published, the TAB's reference to Release 1.5 is out of date. Its open question (general guidance for self- or caregiver-administered vaccines) is the one in tab-flu-01.
recommendation: Ask AIRA to point the TAB's next seasonal update at this guide, and list self- or caregiver-administered vaccines among the topics for future work in 6.4 if tab-flu-01 is not settled in this release.

message: TAB About Technical Advisory Bulletins (Conformance (Table 1)): Reworded. Section 1.5 defines the same verbs except MAY NOT, and does not cite the HL7 Conformance Methodology. Its SHOULD ("may deviate based on local policy, technical constraints, or phased implementation") says more than the TAB's "Recommended to implement", but does not conflict with it.
recommendation: Cite the HL7 v2 Conformance Methodology in 1.5, and add MAY NOT or say that the guide does not use it.

message: TAB About Technical Advisory Bulletins (Local implementation guidance): Partly covered. The guide says each IIS SHOULD publish a local guide and that local profiles SHALL NOT contradict this one, but not that implementers review local guides.
recommendation: Add to 1.1.2 (Scope): "Implementers SHALL review the local implementation guide of each IIS they exchange with."

message: TAB About Technical Advisory Bulletins (For More Information): Missing. Section 6.2 does not say where TABs are published or how to take part.
recommendation: Add to 6.2 where TABs are published (the AIRA repository, TAB resources page) and how to get involved (SISC, or HL7vaxteam@cdc.gov).

message: TAB Messaging Phone and Email; Telecommunication Use Code and Equipment Type Values (Telecommunication Equipment Type (HL70202) Value Set (Table 4)): Partly covered. PH and CP, and the IIS ignoring other types, are covered. The SHOULD NOT for senders (Internet, X.400, fax) is not. IGAMT also lists TDD, TTY, MD, and BP as E, which the TAB does not mention; with s3 ("IIS SHALL ignore other equipment types"), the guide treats as ignorable what the profile treats as an error.
recommendation: Add "Systems SHOULD NOT send equipment types Internet, X.400, or FX" to 4.5.4.3.

message: TAB Messaging Phone and Email; Telecommunication Use Code and Equipment Type Values (Examples): Missing. The guide describes these cases but has none of the examples.
recommendation: Add the TAB's four PID-13 examples to 4.5.4.1 or appendix A.

message: TAB Messaging Phone and Email; Telecommunication Use Code and Equipment Type Values (Not in the TAB): Guide adds. "IIS SHALL accept and store contact information for either the patient or guardian, as appropriate." The TAB does not require IIS to store contact information.

TAB Patient Name (PID-5) Updates to Support Patient Matching (Name type code (HL70200) Value Set usage for PID-5): Reworded. Systems SHOULD support them (s1), as in the TAB, but receiving systems SHALL recognize and process them without error (4.5.2.3 s4), and IIS SHALL recognize 'NB' (4.5.2.6 s2). The TAB makes recognition by the IIS part of a SHOULD.
recommendation: Confirm that the guide means to make recognition of M, N, and NB a SHALL for IIS.

message: TAB Patient Name (PID-5) Updates to Support Patient Matching (Examples: temporary newborn names): Partly covered. The guide refers to Joint Commission and AHIMA conventions but says it "does not prescribe" a format, and gives none of the TAB's examples. The TAB's format is a recommendation, so this is a gap in guidance rather than a conflict.
recommendation: Add the TAB's recommended format and the PID-5 examples to 4.5.2.7 or appendix A.

message: TAB Patient Name (PID-5) Updates to Support Patient Matching (Examples): Missing. The guide has figure 22 of the name types but none of these PID-5 examples.
recommendation: Add the TAB's examples to appendix A, linked from 4.5.2.

message: TAB Patient Name (PID-5) Updates to Support Patient Matching (Not in the TAB): Guide adds. "IIS SHALL accept minor variations in name spelling, case, or special characters when evaluating matches" and "IIS SHALL NOT require submitting systems to alter or 'correct' names to match the registry's stored spelling". The TAB leaves matching out of scope.

TAB Patient Name (PID-5) Updates to Support Patient Matching (Not in the TAB): Guide adds. "IIS MAY define local policies for reconciling capitalization ... but must retain a version of the name as originally submitted." The TAB does not require IIS to keep the submitted form.

section_title: Purpose and Scope of RSP Profiles
message: TAB Query Response Flexibility: Z31 Response for Z34 and Z44 Queries (Background): Partly covered. Section 3.5.1 says RSP content "SHALL be consistent with the profile requested (Z34 or Z44)" and names only Z32 and Z42 as defaults, without saying which responses each query can receive.
recommendation: Add a short table to 3.5.1 or 3.5.2 of the responses each query can receive (Z34 → Z31, Z32, Z33; Z44 → Z31, Z33, Z42).

message: TAB Additional "Unknown" Race and Ethnicity Codes (Tables 1 and 2 (receiving system conformance)): Reworded. The guide makes it a SHALL (IIS SHALL accept the codes, SHALL NOT reject messages because of them), stronger than the TAB's SHOULD. It does not mention translating UNK to an empty value.
recommendation: Confirm that the guide means to raise acceptance from SHOULD to SHALL.

message: TAB Additional "Unknown" Race and Ethnicity Codes (Tables 1 and 2): Missing.
recommendation: Add the TAB's sentence on labels to 4.5.5.2.

message: TAB Additional "Unknown" Race and Ethnicity Codes (Examples): Missing.
recommendation: Add the two examples to appendix A, with the coding system decided in tab-re-03.

message: TAB Additional "Unknown" Race and Ethnicity Codes (Not in the TAB): Guide adds. "IIS SHALL NOT define additional local unknown codes." The TAB does not say this.

section_title: Z33 - Return a Response with No Person Records
message: TAB Returning IIS Patient Immunization Record Information in a Z32 and Z42 RSP (Table 1: Patient types): Partly covered. The guide says a Z33 is returned when a record "cannot be disclosed due to consent or sharing restrictions", and that PD1-12 affects responses, but does not tie the Z33 to PD1-12 = 'Y' or say whether a deceased patient is returned.
recommendation: State in 3.5.2.4 that a patient with PD1-12 'Y' is returned as a Z33, and that a deceased patient MAY be returned.

section_title: Overall Structure of CDS in the RSP
message: TAB Returning IIS Patient Immunization Record Information in a Z32 and Z42 RSP (Table 1: Immunization types (completed, partially administered)): Partly covered. Covered in substance by "Vaccination history order groups SHALL be complete and unfiltered" and the Z32 description, but partially administered doses are not mentioned.
recommendation: Add the TAB's two statements to 3.5.2.2 (Z32) and 3.5.2.5 (Z42).

section_title: Adverse Events Associated With a Specific Vaccination
message: TAB Returning IIS Patient Immunization Record Information in a Z32 and Z42 RSP (Table 1: Observations associated with an immunization): Reworded. The guide says IIS that store an adverse event tied to an immunization SHOULD return it, stronger than the TAB's MAY. It does not address returning eligibility, funding, or VIS (4.4.2.6 only mentions that they can appear in an RSP).
recommendation: Confirm the SHOULD for adverse events, and add MAY statements for eligibility, funding, and VIS in responses.

section_title: Z42 - Return Evaluated Immunization History and Forecast
message: TAB Returning IIS Patient Immunization Record Information in a Z32 and Z42 RSP (Table 1: Clinical decision support): Partly covered. The same gap as the CDS in RSP Alignment comparison (tab-cds-01), which carries the finding.

TAB Returning IIS Patient Immunization Record Information in a Z32 and Z42 RSP (Table 3: PID fields): In narrative only. The guide's disclosure section makes the same point (return only what supports confirmation; mother's maiden name may be used for matching but withheld), with no statements. It does not mention PD1 or NK1 in responses.
recommendation: Add the TAB's field list to 3.5.3 as statements.

message: TAB Returning IIS Patient Immunization Record Information in a Z32 and Z42 RSP (Implications; Table 4): Partly covered. The first point is covered well. Table 4's reading of the verbs for responses (what a querying system can depend on) is not in the guide.
recommendation: Add Table 4, or a sentence on what querying systems can rely on, to 3.5.3.

section_title: Patient Demographic Records and VXUs Without Immunizations
message: TAB Scenarios for Updates and Queries (Table 1: Patient demographic record created or modified): Reworded. The guide requires coordination only before sending demographic-only VXUs "on an ongoing or routine basis"; the TAB requires it whenever a system sends them.
recommendation: Drop "on an ongoing or routine basis" from s2, or confirm that the narrower requirement is intended.

section_title: Official Registry Name Recorded for a Newborn
message: TAB Scenarios for Updates and Queries (Table 1: Legal name modified): Missing. The guide has no row for a name change after the first. It falls under the general demographic MAY (tab-sc-07), but is not named.
recommendation: Confirm the reading with the TAB authors, then add to 3.2.5.7: "When the official registry name is later changed, the submitting system MAY trigger a VXU."

message: TAB Scenarios for Updates and Queries (Appendix, Table 4: Non-identifying vaccination record fields): Partly covered. The guide lists the RXA and RXR fields and "Vaccine information statement and related OBX elements", but not funding source or eligibility, or the LOINC codes. Section 4.6.4 says any field outside the identifying list can be sent as an update, so the meaning is the same.
recommendation: List the four OBX observations with their LOINC codes in 3.2.4.2, as the TAB does.

section_title: Patient Demographic Records and VXUs Without Immunizations
message: TAB Scenarios for Updates and Queries (Not in the TAB): Guide adds. "IIS SHALL accept VXU messages that contain patient demographic information, including VXUs with no immunization events." The TAB leaves IIS processing out of scope and asks submitters to coordinate because some IIS do not accept them.
